# iRender: full LLM context

Generated by tools/llm-docs.sh. Sections: authoring rules, components, core README, then each kit's README. Icon names are in skills/irender/references/icons.md.


---

# Writing iRender documents

iRender renders UI from a JSON or YAML document. This page is the compact set of rules for writing one that validates on the first try. Component props are in `components.md`; each kit's details are in its own file.

## Document

```yaml
version: 1
theme: { tokens: { color: { primary: "#4f46e5" } } }   # optional
state: { count: 0, tab: overview, results: [] }         # optional: browser state, every key you read or set
fragments: { card: { type: stack, children: [] } }      # optional: reusable subtrees
root: { type: stack, children: [] }                     # required: one node
```

Only these five top-level keys exist. Unknown keys are errors.

## Node

```yaml
type: button                 # required: a component name
props: { label: Save }       # the component's props (see components.md); typed and validated
attrs: { id: save, aria-label: Save }   # any HTML attribute; wins over the component's own
class: [cta]                 # extra class names
style: { padding: 12px 20px, ":hover": { opacity: 0.9 }, "@md": { padding: 16 } }
parts: { label: { style: { font-weight: 600 } } }   # style a component's inner elements (names in components.md)
on: { click: { action: set_state, key: count, value: "{{ count + 1 }}" } }
children: []
```

Only these eight keys exist on a node. Components that say `children: no` take none.

## Built-in components (always available)

`element` (any tag via `props.tag`), `text`, `stack`, `button`, `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `list`, `if`, plus `else` and `include`, which the loader resolves.

| kit | flag | adds |
|---|---|---|
| ui-kit | `--ui-kit` | `ui-*` components in the style of shadcn/ui, and a theme with dark mode and theme options |
| chart-kit | `--chart-kit` | `ui-chart`, `ui-sparkline`, `ui-live-data` (Apache ECharts) |
| flow-kit | `--flow-kit` | `ui-flow` and its `ui-flow-*` templates: node-and-edge diagrams |
| icon-kit | `--icon-kit` | `ui-icon`, and icon names in `icon` props of ui-kit components |

Prefer ui-kit components over hand-styled `element`s whenever a kit is in use. They are accessible, themed and dark-mode aware.

## Expressions

Any string may contain `{{ … }}`.

- **Grammar:** paths (`user.name`, `items[0]`, `row['first-name']`, `cart.length`), string, number, boolean and `null` literals, arithmetic `+ - * / %`, comparisons `== != < <= > >=`, `&& || !`, `a ? b : c` and parentheses.
- **Functions:** only `range(n)` / `range(start, end)`, `includes(list, value)` and `toggle(list, value)`. There are no others: no `map`, `filter`, `join`, `toUpperCase`, `Math.*`, template literals or arrow functions.
- **No array or object literals inside `{{ }}`:** write a fixed structure in YAML or JSON instead (`value: { title: Saved, tags: [] }`). Its leaves are **not** evaluated: `value: { description: "Hi {{ name }}" }` stores the text `Hi {{ name }}`. The validator doesn't catch this, so keep expressions out of literal objects and arrays in `set_state`, or set each piece as its own key.
- **Paths only:** `.field` and `[i]` follow paths, not call results (`range(n).length` is invalid).
- **Live or server-side:** a path whose first name is a `state` key updates live in the browser. Any other path is filled from server `data` at render time. Inside a `list`, `item` and `index` (or the `as` / `index` names) are in scope.
- **Exact values:** a string that is only one expression keeps the value's type (`"{{ count }}"` is a number). Mixed text makes a string: `"Buy {{ qty }}"`.

## State and actions

- **Declare state:** every state key an action sets, a control `bind`s or an expression reads live must be declared in `state` with its starting value. Undeclared keys are errors.
- **Top-level keys only:** `bind` and `set_state` `key` take a top-level key, never a path like `draft.customer`. A form needs one flat key per field (`customer`, `product`), which `submit` then gathers in its `body`.
- **Event names:** `on` maps a DOM event (`click`, `input`, `change`, `submit`, `keydown`, …) or `mount` (when the element first appears) to one action or a list. A list runs in order, and `submit` waits for its response.

| action | fields |
|---|---|
| `set_state` | `key`, `value` (usually an expression) |
| `navigate` | `url` |
| `submit` | `endpoint`, `method` (default POST), `body` (object; a query string for GET), `into` (state key for the JSON response) |
| `call` | `name`, `args`: dispatches an `irender:call` DOM event for the host app |
| `wait` | `ms` (at most 60000) |

There is no other action and no inline JavaScript. Anything custom goes through `call`.

- **What gets evaluated:** each field of `submit`'s `body` is evaluated (`body: { customer: "{{ customer }}" }`). So is `call`'s `args`. A `set_state` value is evaluated only when it is one expression string.
- **`submit` failures:** they don't stop the chain. A non-2xx response is still stored in `into`, and a network error fires an `irender:error` DOM event. Either way, the following actions run. Success fires `irender:submitted` with `{ ok, status, data }`. To act only on success, show the outcome with an `if` on the response stored in `into` (e.g. `{{ saved.id }}`), or let the host handle the request through `call`.
- **Forms:** `on.submit` on an `element` with `tag: form` whose actions include `submit` prevents the browser's own navigation.

## Form controls

`input`, `select` and `textarea`, and their `ui-*` versions, take `bind: <state key>` for two-way binding. A checkbox binds a boolean. A radio needs a `value`. `select` / `ui-select` `options` are values or `{ value, label, disabled }`.

## Conditionals and lists

```yaml
- { type: if, props: { when: "{{ step == 1 }}" }, children: [ … ] }
- { type: else, props: { when: "{{ step == 2 }}" }, children: [ … ] }   # else-if; must directly follow an if/else
- { type: else, children: [ … ] }

- type: list
  props: { items: "{{ results }}", as: r, key: "{{ r.id }}", tag: ul }   # key keeps DOM (inputs, focus) across updates
  children: [ { type: text, props: { tag: li, value: "{{ r.title }}" } } ]
```

- `if` adds no element of its own. `list` wraps its items in a `div` unless you give it a `tag` such as `ul` or `tbody`.
- **Mixed conditions:** an `if` inside a server-rendered list may mix the item and state, as in `"{{ filter == null || row.status == filter }}"`. The item part is filled in per row on the server, and the state part stays live.
- Repeat something n times: `items: "{{ range(n) }}"`.
- Keep a set of choices in state: `includes(tags, 'x')` and `toggle(tags, 'x')`.

## Fragments

```yaml
fragments:
  stat:
    type: stack
    children: [ { type: text, props: { value: "{{ label }}" } }, { type: text, props: { value: "{{ value }}" } } ]
root:
  type: stack
  children:
    - { type: include, props: { name: stat, with: { label: Revenue, value: "{{ totals.revenue }}" } } }
```

`name` must be a fixed string. Use fragments for anything repeated more than twice with different values.

## Styles and theme

- **Properties:** `style` accepts any CSS property, in kebab-case. Numbers get `px` where it makes sense.
- **Tokens:** `$group.name` compiles to `var(--group-name)`, and an unknown token is an error. Default tokens:
  - `color.primary`, `primary-hover`, `on-primary`, `surface`, `text`, `muted`, `border`
  - `radius.sm` / `md` / `lg`
  - `space.xs` / `sm` / `md` / `lg` / `xl`
  - `font.body`, `font.size.sm` / `md` / `lg`
- **ui-kit tokens:** the kit adds `color.secondary`, `accent`, `subtle`, `destructive`, `ring` and others. Add your own under `theme.tokens`.
- **Nested blocks:** `":hover"`, `"&.active"`, `"& > li"`, `"@sm"` / `"@md"` / `"@lg"` / `"@xl"` (min-width breakpoints), `"@dark"`, `"@print"`, `"@motion-safe"`, `"@media (…)"`.
- **Dynamic values:** `color: "{{ ok ? 'green' : 'crimson' }}"` updates live. `null` leaves the property unset.
- **Dark mode:** use tokens, not literal colours, so dark mode works. `theme.modes.dark` overrides tokens.

## YAML pitfalls

- **Expressions:** quote any value that starts with `{{` or `{`, or YAML reads it as a mapping. Write `value: "{{ count }}"`, never `value: {{ count }}`.
- **Hex colours:** quote them (`"#4f46e5"`), or `#` starts a comment.
- **Style keys:** quote any key starting with `:`, `@` or `&`, such as `":hover"`, `"@md"` and `"&.active"`.
- **Flow maps:** they are fine for short nodes (`{ type: text, props: { value: Hi } }`). Use block style once a node has children.

## Workflow

1. **Kits:** decide which ones the page needs, and pass the same flags to every command.
2. **Props:** look up each component's props in `components.md` (or run `irender components --ui-kit …`). Don't guess prop names.
3. **Write:** write the document. Put sample server data in a separate `*.data.json` if it reads any.
4. **Validate:** run `irender validate page.yaml --ui-kit …`. It lists every problem with its path, such as `root.children[1].on.click[0].key: 'n' is not declared in 'state'`. Fix them all and repeat until it passes. Treat warnings (unknown CSS) as worth fixing.
5. **Render:** run `irender render page.yaml --data page.data.json --ui-kit … -o page.html`, then open it in a browser to check it.
6. **Untrusted input:** for documents from users or other models, validate and render with `--untrusted`.

## Common mistakes

- **Undeclared state:** setting or binding a key missing from `state`.
- **Unsupported expressions:** JavaScript-only syntax such as `.map(`, `.toFixed(`, `${}`, `===`, `=>`, or `[…]` and `{…}` literals.
- **Missing kit flag:** a `ui-*` component without `--ui-kit` is "unknown component type".
- **Wrong place for a value:** a prop under `attrs`, or an attribute under `props`. Component props go in `props`, and raw HTML attributes such as `id`, `aria-*` and `href` on an `element` go in `attrs`.
- **Children where none are allowed:** giving children to `text`, `input`, `ui-input`, `ui-badge` or other components marked `children: no`. Use `element` or `stack` to group.
- **Bad `else`:** an `else` that doesn't directly follow an `if`, or one that follows a plain `else` (only `else` with `when` can be followed).
- **Layout by hand:** hand-writing flex layout with `element` instead of `stack` (`direction`, `gap`, `align`, `justify`, `wrap`).
- **Literal colours:** they break dark mode. Use `$color.*`.
- **Expressions in literal objects:** `{{ }}` inside a literal object or array in `set_state` stays as text (see Expressions). This is common with toasts: `value: { title: Saved, description: "{{ name }}" }` shows the braces.
- **Toggle groups reset to `null`:** pressing a selected `ui-toggle-group` option again sets its key to `null`, so a filter must treat `null` as "all".
- **Dialogs that stay open:** a submit button inside a `ui-dialog` doesn't close it. Use a `ui-dialog-close` whose `on.click` runs the `submit` (and any toast), so it sends and closes in one click.
- **Missing table components:** `ui-table` has no row or cell components. Its children are `element`s with `tag: thead`, `tbody`, `tr`, `th` and `td`, or a `list` with `tag: tbody`.


---


# Components

Every component with all kits enabled. Each entry: name and summary, then one line per prop (name, type, description), its `parts`, and whether it takes `children`. Core built-ins come first, then `ui-*` (ui-kit), `ui-chart` / `ui-sparkline` / `ui-live-data` (chart-kit), `ui-flow*` (flow-kit) and `ui-icon` (icon-kit).

```
element: Any HTML element. Set attributes with `attrs`.
  tag          tag  HTML tag name (default `div`)
  children: yes
text: Text content.
  value        any (required)  The text. Templates update live when they use `state`.
  tag          tag  HTML tag (default `span`), e.g. `h1`, `p`, `li`
  children: no
stack: Flex layout container.
  direction    one of: row, column, row-reverse, column-reverse  Default `column`
  gap          any  Number (px), CSS length or `$token`
  align        any  `align-items`
  justify      any  `justify-content`
  wrap         bool  Wrap children onto multiple lines
  tag          tag  HTML tag (default `div`)
  children: yes
button: A button. Wire it up with `on.click`.
  label        any  Button text, rendered in the `label` part
  variant      one of: primary, secondary, ghost  Default `primary`
  type         one of: button, submit, reset  Default `button`
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  parts: label
  children: yes
input: Form input.
  bind         statekey  State key kept in sync with the value (`checked` for checkboxes)
  type         string  Input type (default `text`)
  placeholder  any  
  name         string  Form field name (bound radios default to the `bind` key)
  value        any  Initial value when not bound; for a bound radio, the value it stands for
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  children: no
select: Dropdown.
  options      any (required)  Array of values or `{ value, label, disabled }`. Rebuilt in the browser when it uses state.
  bind         statekey  State key kept in sync with the selected value
  placeholder  any  Text of a first, empty option
  name         string  Form field name
  value        any  Initially selected value when not bound
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  children: no
textarea: Multi-line text input.
  bind         statekey  State key kept in sync with the text
  placeholder  any  
  name         string  Form field name
  rows         any  Visible lines (default 3)
  value        any  Initial text when not bound
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  children: no
list: Renders its children once per item. Rebuilt in the browser when `items` uses state.
  items        any (required)  An array: `{{ data.path }}`, or `{{ state_key }}` to rebuild in the browser
  as           string  Name of the current item (default `item`)
  index        string  Name of the current index (default `index`)
  tag          tag  HTML tag (default `div`), e.g. `ul`
  key          any  Per-item key, e.g. `{{ item.id }}`. When the browser rebuilds the list, items whose key survives keep their nodes
  children: yes
if: Renders its children when `when` is truthy. Adds no element of its own. A following `else` (with `when` for else-if) renders when it doesn't.
  when         any (required)  Condition. Shown and hidden in the browser when it uses state.
  children: yes
ui-button: A button in six variants and four sizes. With `href` it is a link that looks like a button.
  label        any  Button text
  icon         any  An icon name (with the icon kit) or a character, before the label
  variant      one of: default, secondary, destructive, outline, ghost, link, brand  Default `default`
  size         one of: default, sm, lg, icon  Default `default`
  href         any  Render a link that looks like a button
  type         one of: button, submit, reset  Default `button`
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  children: yes
ui-badge: A small status label.
  text         any (required)  Badge text
  icon         any  An icon name (with the icon kit) or a character, before the text
  variant      one of: default, secondary, destructive, outline, brand  Default `default`
  children: no
ui-card: A bordered panel with an optional title and description. Put a `ui-card-footer` last for actions.
  title        any  Heading in the card's header
  description  any  Muted text under the title
  tag          tag  HTML tag (default `div`), e.g. `article`, `section`
  parts: header, title, description
  children: yes
ui-card-footer: A row of actions at the bottom of a `ui-card`.
  children: yes
ui-alert: A callout for important messages.
  title        any  Bold first line
  description  any  Body text
  icon         any  An icon name (with the icon kit) or a character, shown on the left, e.g. `warning` or `⚠`
  variant      one of: default, destructive  Default `default`
  parts: icon, title, description
  children: yes
ui-avatar: A round image, or initials when there is none.
  src          any  Image URL
  alt          any  Image description
  fallback     any  Text shown without an image, usually initials
  size         any  Number (px) or CSS length; default 40
  parts: image
  children: no
ui-separator: A thin dividing line.
  orientation  one of: horizontal, vertical  Default `horizontal`
  label        any  Text in the middle of a horizontal line, e.g. `Or continue with`
  decorative   bool  Hide from assistive technology (default true)
  children: no
ui-skeleton: A pulsing placeholder block shown while content loads.
  width        any  Number (px) or CSS length; default 100%
  height       any  Number (px) or CSS length; default 16
  round        bool  A circle instead of a rounded rectangle
  children: no
ui-kbd: A keyboard key.
  text         any (required)  The key, e.g. `⌘K`
  children: no
ui-progress: A progress bar.
  value        any (required)  0–100. Updates live when it uses state.
  parts: indicator
  children: no
ui-aspect-ratio: Keeps its content at a fixed width-to-height ratio.
  ratio        any (required)  Width / height: a number (`1.5`) or `"16 / 9"`
  children: yes
ui-table: A styled table in a scrolling container. Children are the table's rows and sections (`thead`, `tbody`, a `list` with `tag: tbody`, …).
  caption      any  Caption shown under the table
  parts: table
  children: yes
ui-heading: A heading, `h1`–`h4`.
  text         any (required)  The heading
  level        any  1–4 (default 2)
  children: no
ui-text: Body text in one of several typographic styles.
  text         any  The text
  variant      one of: p, lead, large, small, muted, code, blockquote  Default `p`
  tag          tag  Override the variant's tag
  children: yes
ui-spinner: A spinning ring that says something is loading. Takes the text colour.
  size         any  Number (px) or CSS length; default 16
  label        any  What is loading, for screen readers; default `Loading`
  children: no
ui-empty: A placeholder for a page or list with nothing in it yet. Children follow the text, usually a button.
  title        any  What is empty, e.g. `No projects yet`
  description  any  What to do about it
  icon         any  A character or emoji shown above the title
  parts: icon, title, description
  children: yes
ui-scroll-area: A box that scrolls its children, with a thin scrollbar in the theme's colours. It can be focused, so the keyboard scrolls it too.
  height       any  Number (px) or CSS length
  maxHeight    any  Number (px) or CSS length: grows with its content up to this
  label        any  Names the region for screen readers
  children: yes
ui-label: A form label.
  text         any  Label text
  for          any  `id` of the control it labels (or put the control inside)
  children: yes
ui-input: A text field. Same props as `input`.
  bind         statekey  State key kept in sync with the value (`checked` for checkboxes)
  type         string  Input type (default `text`)
  placeholder  any  
  name         string  Form field name (bound radios default to the `bind` key)
  value        any  Initial value when not bound; for a bound radio, the value it stands for
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  children: no
ui-textarea: A multi-line text field. Same props as `textarea`.
  bind         statekey  State key kept in sync with the text
  placeholder  any  
  name         string  Form field name
  rows         any  Visible lines (default 3)
  value        any  Initial text when not bound
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  children: no
ui-select: A dropdown. Same props as `select`.
  options      any (required)  Array of values or `{ value, label, disabled }`. Rebuilt in the browser when it uses state.
  bind         statekey  State key kept in sync with the selected value
  placeholder  any  Text of a first, empty option
  name         string  Form field name
  value        any  Initially selected value when not bound
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  children: no
ui-checkbox: A checkbox with a label.
  label        any  Text next to the box
  bind         statekey  State key holding `true` / `false`
  checked      any  Initially checked, when not bound
  name         string  Form field name
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  parts: control, label
  children: no
ui-switch: An on/off toggle with a label (a checkbox with `role=switch`).
  label        any  Text next to the box
  bind         statekey  State key holding `true` / `false`
  checked      any  Initially checked, when not bound
  name         string  Form field name
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  parts: control, label
  children: no
ui-radio-group: A set of radio buttons for one choice.
  options      any (required)  Array of values or `{ value, label, disabled }`; may use state
  bind         statekey  State key holding the chosen value
  value        any  Initially chosen value, when not bound
  name         string  Form field name (default: the `bind` key)
  orientation  one of: vertical, horizontal  Default `vertical`
  disabled     any  Disable every option
  parts: control, label
  children: no
ui-breadcrumb: Where the current page sits in the site's hierarchy.
  items        any (required)  Array of `{ label, href }`; the last is the current page. May use state
  separator    any  Text between items (default `›`)
  parts: list
  children: no
ui-pagination: Links to the previous, next and nearby pages. Follows `page`, `pages` and `siblings` when they use state.
  page         any (required)  Current page, from 1; may use state, like `pages` and `siblings`
  pages        any (required)  Number of pages
  href         any (required)  Link for page `p`, e.g. `"/orders?page={{ p }}"`
  siblings     any  Pages shown on each side of the current one (default 1)
  parts: list
  children: no
ui-slider: Pick a number by dragging.
  bind         statekey  State key holding the number
  min          any  Default 0
  max          any  Default 100
  step         any  Default 1
  name         string  Form field name
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  children: no
ui-button-group: Buttons joined into one control. Children are usually `ui-button`s; outline ones look best.
  orientation  one of: horizontal, vertical  Default `horizontal`
  label        any  Names the group for screen readers
  children: yes
ui-input-group: A field with text or buttons inside its border. Children are a `ui-input` (or `ui-textarea`, `ui-select`) and any `ui-button`s.
  prefix       any  Text before the field, e.g. `https://` or `$`
  suffix       any  Text after the field, e.g. `.com` or `kg`
  parts: prefix, suffix
  children: yes
ui-field: A label, a control, help text and an error, laid out together. Children are the control, which the label names and the help text and error describe.
  label        any  The label
  for          any  `id` of the control it labels; default the first control inside it
  description  any  Help text under the control
  error        any  An error under the control; hidden while empty, so it can follow state
  orientation  one of: vertical, horizontal  Default `vertical`; `horizontal` puts the control after the label
  parts: label, description, error
  children: yes
ui-accordion: Stacked sections that expand one at a time. Children are `ui-accordion-item`s.
  multiple     bool  Let several items be open at once (default: one at a time)
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  children: yes
ui-accordion-item: One section of a `ui-accordion`.
  title        any (required)  The always-visible heading
  open         any  Start open
  parts: trigger, content
  children: yes
ui-collapsible: Content behind a row that opens and closes it.
  trigger      any (required)  Text of the row that opens and closes it
  open         any  Start open
  parts: trigger, content
  children: yes
ui-tabs: Panels shown one at a time, picked from a row of tabs. Children are `ui-tab-panel`s.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key holding the `value` of the open tab
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  parts: list
  children: yes
ui-tab-panel: One panel of a `ui-tabs`.
  value        any (required)  What `bind` holds when this tab is open
  label        any  Tab text (default: the value)
  children: yes
ui-toggle: A button that stays pressed. `bind` holds whether it is.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key holding `true` / `false`
  label        any  Button text
  variant      one of: default, outline  Default `default`
  size         one of: default, sm, lg  Default `default`
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  children: yes
ui-toggle-group: A row of toggles where one at most is pressed; pressing it again clears it. With `multiple`, any number can be pressed.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key holding the pressed value, or null (a list of them with `multiple`)
  options      any (required)  Array of values or `{ value, label, disabled }`; may use state
  multiple     bool  Let several be pressed; `bind` holds a list
  variant      one of: default, outline  Default `default`
  size         one of: default, sm, lg  Default `default`
  disabled     any  Disable every option
  children: no
ui-theme-toggle: Switches the page between the system's colour scheme, light and dark, and remembers the choice in the browser.
  labels       any  Button text as `{ system, light, dark }`; default System, Light, Dark
  variant      one of: default, outline  Default `outline`
  size         one of: default, sm, lg  Default `sm`
  children: no
ui-theme-option: Picks one choice of a theme option (`theme.options`), such as a palette or a corner radius, for every page, and remembers it in the browser.
  option       string (required)  The theme option it picks, from `theme.options`, e.g. `palette`
  swatch       any  A token each choice is shown with as a colour dot, e.g. `color.primary`, or a list of them
  label        any  The group's name for screen readers (default: the option's label)
  variant      one of: default, outline  Default `outline`
  size         one of: default, sm, lg  Default `sm`
  children: no
ui-theme-panel: A labelled `ui-theme-option` for each theme option (the kits' and the document's), and the mode. Put it in a `ui-popover` for a Theme button.
  options      any  The options to show, in order, e.g. `[palette, radius]` (default: every theme option, the palette first and chart colours last)
  mode         bool  Show the light / dark mode too (default true)
  children: no
ui-theme-colors: Colour inputs for a primary and a second brand colour, typed as hex or picked. Changing one picks the option's `custom` choice; the colours are remembered with the other theme choices.
  option       string  The option whose `custom` choice the colours make (default `palette`)
  children: no
ui-dialog: A modal window. Escape, the ✕ or a click outside closes it.

ui-combobox: A searchable select: one or many values, groups, async options, creatable values, full keyboard support.
  bind         statekey  State key holding the value (an array with `multiple`)
  options      any  Values, `{ value, label, description, disabled }`, or groups `{ label, options }`. From data, or a state path
  valueField   string  Field of an option object holding its value (default `value`)
  labelField   string  Field holding its label (default `label`)
  descriptionField string  Field holding its description (default `description`)
  multiple     bool  Choose several values, shown as removable chips
  searchable   bool  Type to filter (default true)
  clearable    bool  Show a button that clears the value
  creatable    bool  Offer to create a value from what was typed
  searchUrl    any  Load options as you type: GET `<url>?q=<text>`, answering an array
  minChars     number  Characters typed before searching `searchUrl` (default 1)
  debounce     number  Milliseconds to wait after typing before searching (default 250)
  closeOnSelect bool  Close the menu after choosing (default: unless `multiple`)
  hideSelected bool  Leave chosen options out of the menu (default: with `multiple`)
  fixed        any  Values that can't be removed
  value        any  Initial value, when not bound
  placeholder  any  Shown while nothing is chosen (default `Select…`)
  label        any  Accessible name, when no visible label points at `parts.input`
  name         string  Form field name: hidden inputs carry the value(s)
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  loading      any  Show the loading indicator, e.g. `{{ fetching }}`
  noOptionsText any  Default `No options`
  loadingText  any  Default `Loading…`
  createText   any  Default `Create "{input}"`
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  parts: control, input, menu
  children: no

ui-conversation: A scrolling chat log that keeps to its latest message as messages arrive, unless you've scrolled up to read; then a button jumps back down. Children are `ui-message`s, followed by `messages`. Its `parts.bubble`, `parts.avatar` and so on style the messages drawn from `messages`.
  messages     any  Array of messages, after any children. From state, like `{{ messages }}`, it redraws as it changes
  typing       any  Show a typing indicator after the last message, e.g. `{{ waiting }}`
  assistant    any  The typing indicator's sender: `{ name, avatar, initials }`
  empty        any  Text shown while `messages` is empty
  label        any  Names the conversation for screen readers (default `Conversation`)
  height       any  Number (px) or CSS length
  maxHeight    any  Number (px) or CSS length: grows with the messages up to this
  parts: log, empty, latest, avatar, body, meta, bubble, thread, replies
  children: yes
ui-message: One chat message: a bubble with the sender's avatar, name and time, and an optional thread of replies. Children go in the bubble after the text.
  role         one of: assistant, user, system  Who it's from: `assistant` (default, on the left), `user` (on the right) or `system` (centred)
  content      any  The text; line breaks are kept
  name         any  Sender's name, shown above the bubble
  time         any  When it was sent, as text, shown after the name
  avatar       any  Avatar image URL
  initials     any  Shown in the avatar when there's no image
  replies      any  A thread: an array of messages shown under it, folded away behind `N replies`. May use state
  open         bool  Show the thread unfolded
  parts: avatar, body, meta, bubble, thread, replies
  children: yes
ui-typing-indicator: Three bouncing dots that say a reply is on its way. Takes the text colour.
  label        any  What's happening, for screen readers; default `Typing`
  children: no
ui-chat-input: The box a chat message is written in. Enter sends and Shift+Enter starts a new line. Sending appends `{ id, role: user, content }` to `messages`, runs the document's `on.send` actions, and with `endpoint` asks it for the reply, streaming it into a new assistant message; while it streams, the send button stops it. Children go in the toolbar, left of the send button.
  messages     statekey (required)  State key of the messages array: sending appends the user's message, and the reply
  endpoint     any  URL to POST `{ messages }` to. The reply may be JSON (a message, or `{ content }`), plain text, or server-sent events, which stream into the reply as they arrive
  bind         statekey  State key holding the text being written
  waiting      statekey  State key set true from sending until the reply starts: give it to the conversation's `typing`
  placeholder  any  Default `Send a message…`
  label        any  Names the text box for screen readers (default `Message`)
  suggestions  any  Prompts shown while the conversation is empty; clicking one sends it
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  parts: suggestions, box, input, toolbar, send
  children: yes
ui-chart: A chart drawn by Apache ECharts, from rows (`type`, `data`, `x`, `y`) or a full ECharts `option`.
  type         one of: line, area, bar, scatter, effectScatter, pictorialBar, candlestick, boxplot, pie, donut, funnel, radar, heatmap, gauge, tree, treemap, sunburst, sankey, graph, chord, themeRiver, parallel  Series type the shorthand builds; leave it out to use `option` alone
  data         any  Rows (objects or arrays), numbers, or a tree / node list, depending on `type`
  x            any  Field (or column) for categories, names or the x value; default the first
  y            any  Field(s) for values: a field, or a list of fields or `{ field, name, …series options }`; default every other numeric field
  value        any  Third field: heatmap cell value, scatter bubble size
  links        any  `{ source, target, value }` for sankey, graph and chord
  option       any  An ECharts option, merged over what the shorthand builds. `{{ }}` works inside it
  filter       any  Keep rows whose fields match: `{ region: "{{ region }}", date: { from, to }, product: [a, b] }`; blank conditions pass
  aggregate    one of: sum, avg, min, max, count  Group rows by `x` (and `series`)
  series       any  Field whose values become separate series (long-format rows)
  sort         any  A field, `-field` for descending, or a list of them
  limit        any  Keep the first N rows after sorting
  drill        any  Fields to drill through on click, e.g. `[region, country, city]`
  xType        one of: category, time, value, log  The x axis; default: time for dates on lines and points
  zoom         any  Zoom controls along the category or time axis: `inside`, `slider` or `both` (`true`)
  brush        any  Drag to select: `rect` (`true`), `polygon`, `lineX` or `lineY`
  live         any  Live data: `{ url, every, mode: append, window, key, params, paused, stream, pick, into, status }`
  stack        bool  Stack the series
  smooth       bool  Smooth lines
  horizontal   bool  Bars along the x axis
  labels       bool  Show value labels on the marks
  legend       bool  Show the legend (default: with two or more series)
  tooltip      bool  Show a tooltip on hover (default true)
  height       any  Number (px) or CSS length; default 320
  renderer     one of: canvas, svg  Overrides the kit's renderer
  loading      any  Show the loading mask, e.g. `{{ fetching }}`
  bind         statekey  Two-way: the clicked item's name; clicking it again clears it
  bindRow      statekey  The clicked item's row; clicking it again clears it
  bindZoom     statekey  Two-way: the zoom window as `{ from, to }` axis values, or null
  bindLegend   statekey  Two-way: the names of the visible series
  bindBrush    statekey  The rows inside the brushed area
  bindDrill    statekey  Two-way: the drill path, e.g. `[Europe, Germany]`
  maps         any  GeoJSON maps to register first: `{ world: /geo/world.json }`
  group        string  Charts in the same group share tooltips and zoom
  title        any  Accessible name, read before the generated description
  children: no
ui-sparkline: A small chart without axes, for a trend inside text or a stat card.
  data         any (required)  Numbers, or rows with `y`
  y            any  Field holding the value, when `data` has rows
  type         one of: line, area, bar  Default `area`
  height       any  Number (px) or CSS length; default 40
  width        any  Number (px) or CSS length; default 100%
  tooltip      bool  Show the value on hover (default true)
  option       any  An ECharts option, merged over the sparkline's
  live         any  Live data, as for `ui-chart`
  children: no
ui-live-data: Keeps a state key filled from a polled URL, server-sent events or a WebSocket, for any component to read.
  url          any (required)  Polled with GET, or a `ws://` / `wss://` WebSocket; may use state
  into         statekey (required)  State key that holds the data
  every        any  Milliseconds between polls (default 5000, at least 250)
  mode         one of: replace, append  Replace the data with each message (default), or append to it
  window       any  With `append`: keep the last N rows (default 500)
  key          any  With `append`: a row with the same value in this field replaces the old one
  params       any  Query parameters; blank ones are left out, and a change reconnects
  paused       any  Stop while true, e.g. `{{ !liveMode }}`
  stream       bool  Listen to `url` as server-sent events instead of polling
  pick         string  Path to the data in each message, e.g. `data.items`
  status       statekey  State key set to connecting, live, paused or error
  children: no
ui-flow: A diagram of nodes and edges in React Flow's JSON shape. Node and edge types are `ui-flow-node` / `ui-flow-edge` children; `ui-flow-panel` children float above it.
  nodes        any (required)  Nodes as React Flow saves them: `{ id, type, position: { x, y }, data, parentId, width, height, className, style, hidden }`
  edges        any  Edges: `{ id, source, target, sourceHandle, targetHandle, type, label, animated, markerEnd, markerStart, className, style, hidden }`
  layout       any  `layered` places the top-level nodes automatically, ignoring their positions; default: use `position`
  direction    any  `LR` (default), `TB`, `RL` or `BT`: the layout's direction, and where ports without a `side` go
  nodeGap      any  Layout: space between nodes in a rank (default 40)
  rankGap      any  Layout: space between ranks (default 80)
  nodeOrigin   any  Which point of a node `position` names, as fractions: `[0, 0]` top left (default), `[0.5, 0]` top centre
  edgePath     any  Path for edges whose type and template don't name one: `bezier` (default), `straight`, `step` or `smoothstep`
  fit          any  Fit the view to the nodes when they first appear (default true)
  fitPadding   any  Space left around the nodes when fitting, as a fraction of the view (default 0.1)
  viewport     any  The view to start at when `fit` is false: `{ x, y, zoom }`
  center       any  A node id: the view pans to that node whenever this changes
  highlight    any  `neighbors`: while a node is selected, dim everything not connected to it
  selectable   any  Click or Enter selects a node or edge; Shift adds to the selection (default true)
  editable     any  Turns on `draggable`, `connectable` and `deletable` together (default false)
  draggable    any  Nodes can be dragged (default: `editable`)
  connectable  any  Drag from a port to another to connect them; needs `bindEdges` (default: `editable`)
  deletable    any  Delete or Backspace removes the selection; needs `bindNodes` / `bindEdges` (default: `editable`)
  connect      any  Connection rules: `{ sameParent, self, unique, pairs: [{ source, target }] }` (node types)
  newEdge      any  Fields every new edge starts with, e.g. `{ type: smoothstep, markerEnd: arrowclosed }`
  newNode      any  A node (`{ type, data }`) made where a connection is dropped on empty canvas, and joined to it
  confirmDelete any  The id of a dialog to open before deleting; its button sends `flow.delete`
  pan          any  Drag the background to pan (default true)
  zoom         any  Wheel, pinch and keys zoom (default true)
  wheel        any  What the wheel does: `zoom` (default) or `pan` (Ctrl/⌘ + wheel zooms)
  minZoom      any  Default 0.1
  maxZoom      any  Default 2
  background   one of: dots, lines, none  Background pattern (default dots)
  controls     bool  Zoom and fit buttons (default true)
  minimap      bool  An overview in the corner that pans the view (default false)
  height       any  Number (px) or CSS length; default 480. The width is the container's
  title        any  Accessible name
  bind         statekey  State key holding the selected node's id (null when none)
  bindNodes    statekey  State key that gets the nodes, with new positions, after a drag
  bindViewport statekey  State key kept in sync with the view: `{ x, y, zoom }`
  nodeStyles   any  Apply each node's saved `style` and `className` (default true). Turn off when the template works the look out from `data`
  filter       any  Node ids to show; the rest are hidden, except the nodes they connect to, shown as context (`data-neighbor`). Empty or null shows all
  filterNeighbors any  With `filter`, also show the nodes the shown ones connect to (default true)
  search       any  Text to find in the nodes: matches are marked `data-match`, everything else is dimmed
  bindMatches  statekey  State key holding the ids of the nodes `search` matches
  bindHistory  statekey  State key holding how many edits can be undone and redone: `{ undo, redo }`
  bindEdges    statekey  State key that gets the edges after a connection or a deletion
  bindNode     statekey  State key holding the selected node itself (its `id`, `type`, `data`, …), or null: for a side panel that shows or edits it
  bindSelection statekey  State key holding every selected node and edge: `{ nodes: [ids], edges: [ids] }`
  bindDelete   statekey  With `confirmDelete`: what would be deleted, `{ nodes, edges }`, while the dialog is open
  parts: controls, minimap
  children: yes
ui-flow-node: A node type of the `ui-flow` it is in: its children are drawn for every node of that `type`, with the node in scope as `node`. Place `ui-flow-port`s inside.
  type         string  The node type this template draws. Leave it out (or use `default`) for every type no other template declares
  variant      one of: card, plain  `card` (default) gives the node a border, background and padding; `plain` leaves all of it to `style`
  shape        any  The node's outline: `rect`, `rounded`, `pill`, `circle`, `ellipse`, `diamond`, `hexagon`, `parallelogram`, `triangle` or `cylinder`; or `polygon` with `points`. May use the node, e.g. `{{ node.data.shape }}`. Style it through `parts.shape` (`fill`, `stroke`)
  points       any  With `shape: polygon`: the corners as percentages of the box, e.g. `50,0 100,50 50,100 0,50`
  container    bool  Other nodes can sit inside it: dragging a node onto it makes it the node's parent, and off it, takes it out
  resizable    bool  A handle in the bottom-right corner resizes the node; the size is saved as its `width` and `height`
  minWidth     number  Smallest width when resizing (default 80)
  minHeight    number  Smallest height when resizing (default 40)
  parts: shape
  children: yes
ui-flow-edge: An edge type of the `ui-flow` it is in. Its `style` styles the path (`stroke`, `stroke-width`, …); its children, with the edge in scope as `edge`, are the label. Without children the label is `edge.label`.
  type         string  The edge type this template draws. Leave it out (or use `default`) for every type no other template declares
  path         one of: bezier, straight, step, smoothstep  Path shape; default: the edge's own type when it is one of these, else the flow's `edgePath`
  marker       one of: none, arrow, arrowclosed  Arrowhead at the target, unless the edge has `markerEnd`
  markerStart  one of: none, arrow, arrowclosed  Arrowhead at the source, unless the edge has `markerStart`
  animated     bool  Moving dashes, unless the edge sets `animated`
  floating     bool  Attach to the nodes' borders, facing each other, instead of to ports
  parts: label
  children: yes
ui-flow-port: Where edges attach to a node, in a `ui-flow-node`. It is placed on its side of the nearest positioned element: the node, or e.g. a table row with `position: relative`.
  id           any  The port's id, matched against an edge's `sourceHandle` / `targetHandle`. May use the node, e.g. `{{ c.handle }}`
  type         one of: source, target  Edges leave from `source` ports (default) and arrive at `target` ports
  side         any  `left`, `right`, `top` or `bottom`. Default: from the flow's `direction`, e.g. targets left and sources right for `LR`
  offset       any  Where along the side, e.g. `30%` or `24px`. Default: ports on one side share it evenly
  accepts      any  Node types allowed at the other end of a new connection, e.g. `[step, merge]`
  max          any  How many edges this port takes at most
  scope        one of: children  `children`: connects only to nodes inside this node (a container), whatever `sameParent` says
  connectable  any  Whether new connections can start or end here (default true)
  children: no
ui-flow-panel: Content that floats above a `ui-flow`, e.g. a toolbar. It doesn't pan or zoom.
  position     one of: top-left, top-center, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-center, bottom-right  Corner or edge of the flow (default top-left)
  children: yes
ui-flow-item: A palette entry: drag it onto a `ui-flow` to add its `node` there, or click it to add the node in the middle of the view. The flow needs `bindNodes`.
  node         any (required)  The node to add: `{ type, data }`, and `id` if it should keep one
  flow         string  The element id of the flow to add to. Default: the flow it is in, or the page's only flow
  children: yes
ui-icon: An SVG icon from the icon kit's packs, drawn in the current text colour.
  name         string (required)  `pack:icon` (e.g. `logistics:truck`) or a bare `icon`, found in the first pack that has it
  variant      one of: outline, filled  `outline` (default) or `filled`
  size         any  Number (px) or CSS length; default `1em`, the size of the text around it
  label        any  Accessible name. Without one the icon is decorative and hidden from screen readers
  children: no
```


---


# iRender

[![CI](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

Build UI from configuration. Write a document in JSON or YAML, then validate it and render it to HTML with a ~4.5 KB (gzipped) runtime for state and actions.

```sh
cargo run -p irender-cli -- render examples/product.json --data examples/product.data.json -o product.html
cargo run -p irender-cli -- validate examples/counter.yaml
cargo run -p irender-cli -- components   # built-in components and their props
cargo run -p irender-cli -- schema       # JSON Schema for documents
```

See [`examples/`](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/examples/README.md) for complete pages: a dashboard built from fragments, a live API search, a multi-step form and a storefront whose config is partly generated in Rust. To browse them all, run `examples/build.sh`, then `python3 examples/serve.py` (a static server plus the live endpoints the chart gallery uses).

## Writing documents with an LLM

- **[`llms.txt`](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/llms.txt)** is an index of the docs for models, and [`llms-full.txt`](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/llms-full.txt) puts all of them in one file to paste into a context window.
- **[`skills/irender`](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/skills/irender/SKILL.md)** is an [Agent Skill](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview) that writes, validates and renders documents. It's linked into `.claude/skills` here. To use it in another project, copy the folder into that project's `.claude/skills/` or into `~/.claude/skills/`.
- **The validation loop:** both tell the model to check its output with `irender validate`, which reports every problem at its path, so it can fix them all before rendering. For documents a model writes for end users, validate and render with `--untrusted`.
- **Regenerating:** `tools/llm-docs.sh` regenerates the component and icon references, the copies of the READMEs and examples, and `llms-full.txt` from the CLI and the sources. `tools/llm-docs.sh --check` fails when they're stale. The hand-written sources are `llms.txt`, `skills/irender/SKILL.md` and `skills/irender/references/authoring.md`.

## Crates

| crate | role |
|---|---|
| `irender-core` | Document model (serde), expressions, theme tokens, policy, validation → IR. No HTML. |
| `irender-style` | Compiles style blocks into hashed, deduplicated classes in cascade layers; CSS validation and minification via lightningcss. |
| `irender-html` | Server-side renderer, component registry, built-ins, browser runtime. No web-framework dependency. |
| `irender-cli` | `validate`, `render` (with `--timings`, `--repeat`, `--parallel`, `--minify`, `--ui-kit`, `--chart-kit`, `--flow-kit`, `--icon-kit`, `--icons`), `schema`, `components`, `icons`. |
| `irender-ui-kit` | Optional, shadcn-style components (`ui-button`, `ui-card`, `ui-alert`, form controls, table, pagination, a sidebar layout, …) and a matching theme. See its [README](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-ui-kit/README.md). |
| `irender-chart-kit` | Optional charts drawn by Apache ECharts: `ui-chart` (shorthand for 22 series types, or any ECharts option), `ui-sparkline` and `ui-live-data`: filters, grouping and drill-downs in the browser, clicks, zoom, legend and brush as state, live polling, SSE and WebSocket data, themed from the document's tokens. See its [README](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-chart-kit/README.md). |
| `irender-icon-kit` | Optional `ui-icon`: original SVG icons, outline and filled, in packs (core, arrows, status, logistics, warehouse, retail, manufacturing, accounting, agriculture, automotive, aviation, banking, construction, education, energy, finance, healthcare, hospitality, hr, insurance, it, legal, marketing, maritime, media, mining, oil-gas, public-sector, robotics, simulation, social, space, sports, telecom) drawn to one standard, a `brands` pack of social and sign-in logo marks, plus your own packs from SVG files, sanitized on load. See its [README](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-icon-kit/README.md). |
| `irender-flow-kit` | Optional `ui-flow`: node-and-edge diagrams from React Flow's JSON, with node and edge types written as ordinary iRender trees, ports from node data, layered layout, pan and zoom, selection, dragging, connecting with rules, deleting with confirmation, a palette, containers, copy and paste, undo, search and a minimap. See its [README](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-flow-kit/README.md). |

## A node

```json
{
  "type": "button",
  "props": { "label": "{{ qty == 1 ? 'Buy now' : 'Buy ' + qty }}", "disabled": "{{ qty < 1 }}" },
  "attrs": { "id": "buy", "aria-label": "Buy", "data-sku": "{{ product.sku }}" },
  "class": ["cta"],
  "style": {
    "padding": "12px 20px",
    "background": "$color.primary",
    "width": "{{ qty * 10 }}%",
    ":hover": { "transform": "translateY(-1px)" },
    "@md": { "padding": 16 },
    "@dark": { "box-shadow": "none" }
  },
  "parts": { "label": { "style": { "font-weight": 600 } } },
  "on": { "click": { "action": "set_state", "key": "qty", "value": "{{ qty + 1 }}" } }
}
```

- **props** are typed per component and validated.
- **attrs** accept any HTML attribute and override the component's defaults.
- **style** accepts any CSS property, including nested `:pseudo`, `&selector`, `@breakpoint`, `@variant` and `@media …` blocks. Numbers get `px` where it makes sense, and `$tokens` compile to `var(--…)`.
- **parts** style a component's inner elements.
- **on** maps DOM events to declarative actions: `set_state`, `navigate`, `submit`, `call` and `wait`. A `call` dispatches an `irender:call` DOM event for the host app to handle. A `wait` (`{ "action": "wait", "ms": 3000 }`, at most 60 000) pauses before the next action, e.g. to hide a message again.
- **Expressions** (`{{ … }}`) support paths, literals, arithmetic, comparisons, `&& || !`, `?:` and the functions `range`, `includes` and `toggle`. An expression that references `state` updates live in the browser. Any other path is filled in from server `data` at render time.
  - `range(n)` is the list `[0, 1, …, n - 1]`, and `range(start, end)` runs from `start` to `end - 1`, for a `list` that repeats something a number of times: `"items": "{{ range(stars) }}"`.
  - Arguments are truncated to whole numbers, and anything that isn't a number counts as 0.
  - At most 1000 items.
  - `includes(list, value)` says whether the list has the value (compared as `==`), and `toggle(list, value)` is the list without it if it has it, or with it added at the end. Together they keep a set of choices in state: a button whose `aria-pressed` is `"{{ includes(tags, 'rust') }}"` and whose click sets `tags` to `"{{ toggle(tags, 'rust') }}"`. Anything not a list counts as empty.
  - These are the only functions. `.field` and `[i]` follow paths only, so `range(n).length` isn't allowed.
  - In `style`, a value from an expression is set on the element itself: `null` (or a value that's dropped as unsafe) leaves the property as if it weren't declared, never taking a parent's value, and `inherit`, `initial`, `unset` and `revert` work. Under `:hover`, a media query or a nested selector those keywords count as no value.
- **Built-in components:** `element`, `text`, `stack`, `button`, `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `list` and `if`. Run `irender components` for their props. `include` and `else` are handled by the resolver; see below.
- **Cascade order:** theme variables → `i-base` layer (component defaults) → `i-instance` layer (the document's `style`). The document always wins.

### Theme

A document's `theme` sets design tokens (`$color.primary` in styles is `var(--color-primary)`), `modes` that override them under a variant (`dark`), `breakpoints` and `variants`. `options` are sets of overrides people choose between on the page: a palette, a corner radius, a density.

```yaml
theme:
  tokens: { color: { primary: "#4f46e5" } }
  options:
    palette:
      label: Colour
      default: indigo
      choices:
        indigo: { tokens: { color: { primary: "#4f46e5" } } }
        rose:
          label: Rose
          tokens: { color: { primary: "#e11d48" } }
          modes: { dark: { color: { primary: "#fb7185" } } }
```

- A choice applies through `data-theme-<option>` on `<html>` (`data-theme-palette="rose"`); its `modes` give its own values under a variant, so a palette has its own dark colours. A token a choice sets without a dark value keeps it in dark mode.
- The default choice (`default`, or the first) is part of the base tokens: a page with nothing chosen looks like it.
- Option and choice names use lowercase letters, digits and `-`. Mistakes are reported with their paths, like other theme errors.
- [irender-ui-kit](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-ui-kit/README.md#theme-options) ships options (palette, radius, density, text size, font) and `ui-theme-option`, which picks one, remembers it and applies it before the page shows. The [chart kit](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-chart-kit/README.md#theme) adds chart colour schemes. A document adds choices to these or options of its own.

## Form controls

`input`, `select` and `textarea` take `bind: <state key>` to keep a state value in sync both ways.

```json
{ "type": "select", "props": { "bind": "country", "placeholder": "Country",
  "options": [{ "value": "in", "label": "India" }, { "value": "de", "label": "Germany", "disabled": true }] } }
{ "type": "input", "props": { "type": "radio", "bind": "size", "value": "m" } }
{ "type": "input", "props": { "type": "checkbox", "bind": "gift" } }
{ "type": "textarea", "props": { "bind": "notes", "rows": 4 } }
```

- **`select`:** `options` is an array of plain values or `{ value, label, disabled }`. If it comes from server data, the options are fixed. If it reads `state`, the browser rebuilds them when the array changes and keeps the current choice. `placeholder` adds a first, empty option that shows while the key is empty.
- **Radios:** a bound radio needs a `value`. It is checked when the state equals that value, and choosing it writes the value. Radios bound to the same key share `name` automatically, so the browser keeps one checked.
- **Checkboxes:** a bound checkbox stores `true` / `false`.
- **Types:** the DOM holds option and radio values as text. If a key starts out as a number, choosing a radio or option keeps it a number, as a `number` input does. Otherwise it becomes a string.

## Dynamic content

Parts of a page can come from API calls or other runtime work in four ways. Pick by *when* the data is known.

| known when | use |
|---|---|
| the request comes in | server `data`: `engine.render(&ir, &data)`. `{{ path }}`, `list` and `if` read it. The document is loaded once and reused. |
| the document is loaded | `include` fragments built by your code (below), or build the whole `Document` in code and call `engine.resolve(&doc)`. |
| after the page loads, in the browser | `submit` with `into` stores a JSON response in `state`. Text, attributes, `if` and `list` that use that key update. |
| the page opens | `on: { mount: … }` runs actions as soon as an element appears. |

### `if`

```json
{ "type": "if", "props": { "when": "{{ user.admin }}" }, "children": [ … ] }
```

It renders its children only when `when` is truthy, and adds no element of its own. A condition that only reads server `data` is decided on the server and leaves nothing behind. A condition that reads `state` puts the content between two empty `<template>` markers, and the runtime moves it in and out of the page as the condition changes. The markers are valid anywhere, including inside `<table>` and `<ul>`. Hidden content keeps its DOM nodes, so input values and listeners survive being hidden. Note that the markers count as siblings for `:first-child` / `:nth-child`.

An `else` right after an `if` renders its children when the `if` doesn't. Give it a `when` to make it an else-if, and chain as many as you like; a plain `else` ends the chain:

```json
{ "type": "if", "props": { "when": "{{ n > 2 }}" }, "children": [ … ] },
{ "type": "else", "props": { "when": "{{ n > 0 }}" }, "children": [ … ] },
{ "type": "else", "children": [ … ] }
```

The resolver turns each `else` into an `if` whose condition is that no earlier branch matched, so it behaves exactly like one, including updating live when a condition reads `state`. An `else` takes only `when` and children, and must directly follow an `if` or an `else` with `when`.

### Lists that change in the browser

When `items` reads `state`, `list` also writes its children once into a `<template>` as its first child. When the array changes, the runtime rebuilds every item from that template. The server still renders the initial items, so the page is complete without JavaScript.

```json
{ "version": 1,
  "state": { "results": [], "loading": false },
  "root": { "type": "stack", "children": [
    { "type": "element",
      "on": { "mount": [
        { "action": "set_state", "key": "loading", "value": true },
        { "action": "submit", "method": "GET", "endpoint": "/api/search", "into": "results" },
        { "action": "set_state", "key": "loading", "value": false } ] } },
    { "type": "if", "props": { "when": "{{ loading }}" },
      "children": [{ "type": "text", "props": { "value": "Loading…" } }] },
    { "type": "list", "props": { "items": "{{ results }}", "as": "r", "tag": "ul" },
      "children": [{ "type": "text", "props": { "tag": "li", "value": "{{ r.title }}" },
                     "on": { "click": { "action": "call", "name": "open", "args": { "id": "{{ r.id }}" } } } }] } ] } }
```

Inside a rebuilt item, `item` and `index` (or your `as` / `index` names) are known only in the browser. They work in everything that updates live: text, attributes, classes, `{{ }}` style values, `if`, nested `list` and action arguments. Props that a component reads once on the server, such as `tag`, `variant` or `type`, cannot depend on them. Actions in a list run one after another, and `submit` waits for its response, so `loading` flags work as shown above.

Without a `key`, every item is rebuilt when the array changes, so focus and typed input inside an item are lost. Give `list` a `key` (e.g. `"key": "{{ r.id }}"`) and an item whose key is still in the new array keeps its DOM nodes: input values, focus and hidden `if` content survive, `mount` doesn't run again, and only text and attributes that read the item or `index` update. Items are moved only when they're out of order. Keys should be unique; a repeated key reuses one old item per occurrence. A keyed list's server-rendered items are replaced by template items when the page starts, because the server baked their values into plain HTML.

### `mount` actions

`on: { mount: … }` runs when the element first appears: at page start, or when an `if` shows it or a list rebuilds it. A server-rendered element mounts once. The name doesn't clash with `<img>`'s native `load` event, which still works through `on: { load: … }`.

### `include`

```json
{ "version": 1,
  "fragments": { "card": { "type": "stack", "children": [ { "type": "text", "props": { "value": "{{ item.name }}" } } ] } },
  "root": { "type": "list", "props": { "items": "{{ products }}" },
            "children": [{ "type": "include", "props": { "name": "card" } }] } }
```

An `include` node is replaced by its fragment when the document is loaded. The fragment is validated like the rest of the document, with paths such as `root.children[0]@card.props.value`, and it sees the scope it's included in. Fragments are looked up in the document's `fragments` first, then in `engine.fragments`:

```rust
use irender_core::{FragmentDir, NodeSpec};

engine.fragments = Some(Arc::new(FragmentDir("ui/fragments".into())));   // <name>.json / .yaml; CLI: --fragments DIR
// or build them from anything known at load time:
engine.fragments = Some(Arc::new(move |name: &str| -> Result<Option<NodeSpec>, String> {
    match name {
        "promo" => Ok(Some(serde_json::from_value(fetch_promo_config()?).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?)),
        _ => Ok(None),
    }
}));
```

`include` takes `props.name`, which must be a fixed name, and optionally `props.with`. An error from your source is reported at the include's path. Cycles are rejected, and nesting, including fragments, is limited to `MAX_DEPTH` (64) levels. Fragments are expanded at load time, so a fragment that changes per request means loading per request. Loading costs tens of µs for typical documents (see Performance). Cache the `Ir` per fragment version if that matters.

#### Parameters

`with` passes values into the fragment, so one fragment serves different data:

```yaml
fragments:
  stat:
    type: stack
    children:
      - { type: text, props: { value: "{{ label }}" } }
      - { type: text, props: { value: "{{ value }}" }, style: { color: "{{ tone }}" } }
root:
  type: stack
  children:
    - { type: include, props: { name: stat, with: { label: Revenue, value: "{{ totals.revenue }}", tone: $color.primary } } }
    - { type: include, props: { name: stat, with: { label: In cart, value: "{{ cart.length }}", tone: green } } }
```

A parameter is substituted into the fragment's expressions when the document loads. Inside the fragment above, `{{ value }}` becomes the caller's `{{ totals.revenue }}`, so it behaves exactly as if written in place:
- Server data is filled in on the server.
- An argument that reads state, like `{{ cart.length }}`, keeps updating in the browser.
- An `item` from a list, including one the browser rebuilds, still resolves.

Literal arguments stay literal, so the usual checks apply to them: prop types, `bind` keys, URL policy, and CSS tokens and values. A parameter that is a path or a literal object can be read further (`{{ user.name }}` with `with: { user: "{{ order.customer }}" }`); a computed one (`"{{ a + b }}"`) can't.

Names the fragment uses but no `with` passes are looked up at render time as usual, so fragments can still read the scope they're included in. Defaults are expressions: `{{ size || 'md' }}`. A parameter the fragment never uses gives a warning, which catches typos. A `list` inside the fragment whose `item` or `index` name matches a parameter is an error, since it would hide the parameter.

## Policies

`Engine::new()` trusts the document. `Engine::untrusted()` (or `--untrusted` in the CLI) is for user- or LLM-written configs. It blocks `on*` attributes, `javascript:` URLs, dangerous tags and CSS `expression()`. CSS values that could break out of their declaration are always rejected. So are `data-i-*` attributes, which the runtime reads its bindings and actions from.

lightningcss reports unknown CSS properties and invalid values as **warnings**, because it doesn't know every valid property. Standard properties it doesn't model, such as `border-collapse`, `float` or `pointer-events`, are on an allowlist in `irender-style/src/validate.rs`. Their names are accepted, but their values aren't checked. Use `strict_css` (`--strict-css` in the CLI) to make them errors.

## Performance

```sh
cargo bench -p irender-html                                  # criterion; filter with: -- render/table
cargo bench -p irender-html --features parallel              # adds render/html_parallel/*
cargo run --release -p irender-cli -- render doc.json --data data.json --repeat 200 -o out.html
```

`--timings` / `--repeat N` print parse, resolve, render and serialize times for your own document. Load (parse + resolve) is meant to happen once per document change. Render happens per request.

Results on an Apple M4 Pro, release build (measured 2026-11-17):

| fixture | load | render | per element | render, parallel |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| product example (17 elements) | 75 µs | 56 µs | ~3.3 µs | — |
| table, 100 rows (~500 elements) | 32 µs | 442 µs | ~0.88 µs | 210 µs |
| table, 1000 rows (~5000 elements) | 32 µs | 4.24 ms | ~0.85 µs | 1.06 ms |
| 1000 cards with unique styles (~2000 elements) | 5.6 ms | 2.88 ms | ~1.4 µs | — |
| 50 nested levels | 104 µs | 24 µs | ~0.47 µs | — |

**Load** is parse + resolve + CSS validation. **Render, parallel** uses `parallel_min_items = Some(64)`; "—" means the document has no list that large, so it renders on one thread with no overhead.

What keeps rendering fast:
- **Styles are cached by content.** A style block already compiled in this render costs one hash and one comparison (~0.3 µs instead of ~1.4 µs). Built-in components' default styles are built once per process.
- **Browser data is written straight to the output.** Bindings and actions are folded and serialized directly into the HTML, without building intermediate JSON values.
- **Elements borrow from the node.** An element borrows its node's attributes, classes, styles and actions instead of copying them.

`--minify` costs about as much as rendering a small page and saves ~17% of the CSS.

Documents can nest at most ~60 UI levels, and at most 64 counting included fragments. Deeper input is rejected with a located error, which stops hostile input from overflowing the stack.

## Concurrency

**Across requests.** `Engine` and `Ir` are `Send + Sync` (checked at compile time), and `Engine::render` takes `&self` and `&Ir`. Load a document once and render it from any number of threads or async tasks without locks:

```rust
let engine = Arc::new(Engine::new());
let ir = Arc::new(engine.load(src, Format::Json)?);
// in each request handler:
let page = engine.render(&ir, &request_data)?;
```

**Within one page.** With the `parallel` feature, lists with at least `parallel_min_items` items render in chunks on rayon's thread pool:

```rust
let engine = Engine { parallel_min_items: Some(64), ..Engine::new() };  // CLI: --parallel 64
```

The output is byte-identical to a single-thread render, and the first error in document order is reported. This lowers the latency of a large page but uses slightly more total CPU. On a server that is already busy, every core is serving some request, so parallel rendering is off by default. Turn it on when large pages are rare and their latency matters, such as reports, exports or admin tables.

## Features

| crate | feature | default | effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `irender-core` | `yaml` | yes | Accept `.yaml` / `.yml` documents. |
| `irender-style` | `lightningcss` | yes | Validate CSS declarations and allow `--minify`. |
| `irender-html` | `lightningcss`, `yaml` | yes | Forward to the crates above. |
| `irender-html` | `parallel` | no | Parallel list rendering (`rayon`). The CLI enables it. |

## Tests

```sh
cargo test                                            # everything (the CLI enables `parallel`, so its tests run too)
cargo test -p irender-html                               # renderer without `parallel`
cargo test -p irender-html --features parallel           # renderer with `parallel`
cargo test -p irender-html --test browser -- --ignored   # drives the example in headless Chrome (CHROME=… to override)
```

The browser tests run in WebKit and Firefox too, through a stand-in for Chrome built on Playwright:

```sh
npm ci --prefix tools/playwright && npx --prefix tools/playwright playwright-core install webkit firefox
BROWSER=webkit CHROME=$PWD/tools/playwright/dump-dom.js cargo test --workspace --test browser -- --ignored   # or BROWSER=firefox
```

| suite | covers |
|---|---|
| `irender-core` unit tests + `tests/core.rs` | expressions and type conversions, error paths, JSON vs YAML, prop/style/action/theme validation, untrusted policy, warnings |
| `irender-style` unit tests + `tests/compile.rs` | nesting, selector variants, dynamic values, layer order, dark-mode variables, cache, pinned class names |
| `irender-html/tests/components.rs` | every built-in, `if` markers and `else` chains, list item templates, `include` (scope, sources, cycles, depth, `FragmentDir`), which values update live, actions, URL and `</script>` safety, deterministic output, custom components, rendering from many threads, parallel output identical to sequential |
| `irender-html/tests/runtime_parity.rs` | the browser runtime has its own copy of the expression evaluator; ~90 expressions run through both (Rust, and JS via `node`), and any disagreement fails. Skips with a message if `node` isn't installed. |
| `irender-html/tests/browser.rs` | opt-in, needs Chrome: clicks, types and checks the DOM of the product example; toggles `if` blocks, rebuilds lists from state, runs item-scoped and `mount` actions; binds radios, checkboxes, selects (with options from state) and textareas |

## Custom components

```rust
use irender_html::{Component, Engine, RenderCx, RenderError};
use irender_core::{ComponentInfo, Node, PropDef, PropKind};

struct Badge;
impl Component for Badge {
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str { "badge" }
    fn info(&self) -> ComponentInfo {
        const PROPS: &[PropDef] = &[PropDef::new("text", PropKind::Any, "").required()];
        ComponentInfo { doc: "A badge", props: PROPS, parts: &[], children: false, open_props: false }
    }
    fn render(&self, node: &Node, cx: &mut RenderCx<'_>) -> Result<(), RenderError> {
        let mut el = cx.element("span", node);
        if let Some(text) = node.prop("text") {
            el.text(text);
        }
        cx.open(&el, node)?;
        cx.close("span");
        Ok(())
    }
}

let mut engine = Engine::new();
engine.registry.register(Badge);
```

### Page-level CSS and client behaviours

A component that needs more than per-element styles and the built-in actions can add two kinds of page-level code. Both take `&'static str`, so they come from component code and never from a document:

- `cx.global_css(name, css)` adds a rule such as `@keyframes` once per page, however many instances ask for it.
- `cx.global_js(name, js)` adds a client behaviour's script once per page. `el.behavior(name, config)` marks an element for it. The runtime starts the behaviour on each marked element, including ones an `if` or a rebuilt list inserts later, and calls its `update` after every state change:

```js
(window.__irenderBehaviors ||= {})["counter"] = (el, api) => {
  // api.config (from `behavior`), api.state, api.set(key, value), api.emit(event, detail)
  el.addEventListener("click", () => api.set("n", api.state.n + api.config.step));
  return { update(state) { el.textContent = state.n; } };
};
```

- `cx.early_js(name, js)` adds a script once per page that runs right after the page's `<style>`, before any content is shown. Use it only for what must happen before the first paint. `ui-theme-toggle` uses it to apply a stored colour scheme without a flash.
- `registry.early_js(name, js)` adds such a script to every page rendered with that registry, whatever components it uses. A kit uses it for a setting that covers the whole page: `irender-ui-kit` applies the colour scheme chosen with `ui-theme-toggle` on every page, with a toggle on it or not.

Documents can't mark elements themselves: `data-i-*` attributes are reserved. `irender-ui-kit`'s `ui-combobox` is built this way.

### Passing values to nested components

- `cx.with_context(name, value, f)` makes a `Val` available to the components rendered inside `f`, and `cx.context(name)` reads the innermost one. Documents can't read or set it. A value that depends on an item only the browser knows stays a template, so a dialog can hand its id to the close buttons inside it, even in a list the browser rebuilds.
- `cx.scope_key()` tells the items of a server-rendered list apart, for element ids. Inside a list the browser rebuilds, `cx.client_key()` is a template of the surrounding list indexes (`{{ index }}`) to add as well.


---


# irender-ui-kit

Ready-made components for [iRender](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/README.md) documents, styled after [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/). Every component is plain config, and nothing needs JavaScript beyond iRender's own runtime. Overlays use the browser's own `<dialog>`, invoker commands, Popover API and CSS anchor positioning.

```rust
let mut engine = irender_html::Engine::new();
irender_ui_kit::register(&mut engine.registry);

let mut doc = irender_core::parse(src, irender_core::Format::Yaml)?;
irender_ui_kit::apply_theme(&mut doc);   // optional: the kit's neutral palette, dark mode included
let ir = engine.resolve(&doc)?;
```

From the CLI, add `--ui-kit` to `validate`, `render` or `components`:

```sh
cargo run -p irender-cli -- render examples/ui-kit/gallery.yaml --ui-kit -o gallery.html
cargo run -p irender-cli -- components --ui-kit      # every component and its props
```

```yaml
- type: ui-card
  props: { title: Create project, description: Deploy your new project in one click. }
  children:
    - { type: ui-input, props: { bind: name, placeholder: Project name } }
    - type: ui-card-footer
      children:
        - { type: ui-button, props: { label: Cancel, variant: outline } }
        - { type: ui-button, props: { label: Deploy } }
```

## Components

| component | props | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-button` | `label`, `icon`, `variant` (default, secondary, destructive, outline, ghost, link, brand), `size` (default, sm, lg, icon), `href`, `type`, `disabled` | With `href` it renders a link that looks like a button. Children follow the label. |
| `ui-badge` | `text`, `icon`, `variant` (default, secondary, destructive, outline, brand) | |
| `ui-card` | `title`, `description`, `tag` | Parts: `header`, `title`, `description`. |
| `ui-card-footer` | | A row of actions; put it last in a card. |
| `ui-alert` | `title`, `description`, `icon`, `variant` (default, destructive) | `role="alert"`. Parts: `icon`, `title`, `description`. |
| `ui-empty` | `title`, `description`, `icon` | A placeholder for a page or list with nothing in it yet; children (usually buttons) follow the text. Parts: `icon`, `title`, `description`. |
| `ui-avatar` | `src`, `alt`, `fallback`, `size` | Initials when there's no `src`. |
| `ui-separator` | `orientation`, `decorative`, `label` | With `label`, a horizontal line with text in the middle, like "Or continue with". |
| `ui-skeleton` | `width`, `height`, `round` | Pulses gently; still for people who ask their system for reduced motion. |
| `ui-spinner` | `size` (default 16), `label` (default `Loading`) | A spinning ring in the text colour, `role="status"`. Slows down for people who ask for reduced motion. |
| `ui-kbd` | `text` | |
| `ui-progress` | `value` (0–100) | Updates live when `value` uses state, and is clamped to 0–100 in CSS. |
| `ui-aspect-ratio` | `ratio` (`1.5` or `"16 / 9"`) | Its children fill it. |
| `ui-table` | `caption` | Children are the table's rows and sections, so `list` with `tag: tbody` works. Part: `table`. |
| `ui-scroll-area` | `height`, `maxHeight`, `label` | Scrolls its children with a thin scrollbar in the theme's colours. Focusable, so the keyboard scrolls it; `label` makes it a named region. |
| `ui-heading` | `text`, `level` (1–4) | |
| `ui-text` | `text`, `variant` (p, lead, large, small, muted, code, blockquote), `tag` | Takes children, e.g. inline `code`. |
| `ui-label` | `text`, `for` | Takes children, so it can wrap a control. |
| `ui-field` | `label`, `for`, `description`, `error`, `orientation` (vertical, horizontal) | A label, the control (its children), help text and an error. The label names the control, and the control's `aria-describedby` points at the help text and error, so screen readers read them with it. The control is the one whose id is `for`, or else the first control inside, which gets an id if it has none. The error is hidden while empty, so `"{{ … ? 'Too short' : '' }}"` shows it only when needed, and it is announced when it appears. Parts: `label`, `description`, `error`. |
| `ui-input-group` | `prefix`, `suffix` | Text or buttons inside one field's border: children are a `ui-input` (or `ui-textarea`, `ui-select`) and any `ui-button`s. The group shows the focus ring and the invalid border. Parts: `prefix`, `suffix`. |
| `ui-button-group` | `orientation` (horizontal, vertical), `label` | Buttons joined into one control (`role="group"`); outline buttons look best. |
| `ui-input`, `ui-textarea`, `ui-select` | same as `input`, `textarea`, `select` | Same binding behaviour as the built-ins, restyled. |
| `ui-checkbox`, `ui-switch` | `label`, `bind`, `checked`, `name`, `disabled` | The switch is a checkbox with `role="switch"`. Parts: `control`, `label`. |
| `ui-radio-group` | `options`, `bind`, `value`, `name`, `orientation`, `disabled` | Options are values or `{ value, label, disabled }`, and may come from state. |
| `ui-breadcrumb` | `items` (`{ label, href }`), `separator` | The last item is the current page. `items` may come from state. |
| `ui-pagination` | `page`, `pages`, `href`, `siblings` | `href` is evaluated per page with `p` in scope: `"/orders?page={{ p }}"`. `page`, `pages` and `siblings` may come from state. |
| `ui-slider` | `bind`, `min`, `max`, `step`, `name`, `disabled` | A range input; `bind` holds a number. |
| `ui-accordion` + `ui-accordion-item` | accordion: `multiple`, `id`; item: `title`, `open` | Native `<details>`. One item open at a time unless `multiple`. |
| `ui-collapsible` | `trigger`, `open` | Native `<details>`. |
| `ui-tabs` + `ui-tab-panel` | tabs: `bind` (required), `id`; panel: `value`, `label` | `bind` holds the open panel's `value`. Tabs carry `role=tab`, `aria-selected`, `aria-controls`. |
| `ui-toggle` | `bind`, `label`, `variant` (default, outline), `size`, `disabled` | `aria-pressed` follows `bind`. |
| `ui-toggle-group` | `bind`, `options`, `multiple`, `variant`, `size`, `disabled` | One option pressed at most; pressing it again sets `bind` to null. With `multiple`, `bind` holds a list and each press adds or removes its option. |
| `ui-theme-toggle` | `labels` (`{ system, light, dark }`), `variant` (default `outline`), `size` (default `sm`) | System / Light / Dark.
