Light and Dark override `prefers-color-scheme` for the theme's dark mode and `@dark` styles; the choice is kept in `localStorage` (`irender-theme`) and applied before the page is shown, so a reload doesn't flash. Every page rendered with the kit applies it, with a toggle on it or not. Its behaviour is added only to pages that use it. |
| `ui-theme-option` | `option` (required), `swatch` (a token, or a list for several dots), `label`, `variant` (default `outline`), `size` (default `sm`) | Picks a choice of a theme option for every page; see [Theme options](#theme-options). |
| `ui-theme-panel` | `options` (default: every theme option), `mode` (default true) | A labelled `ui-theme-option` per option, palette first and chart colours last, and the mode. Put it in a `ui-popover` for a Theme button. |
| `ui-theme-colors` | `option` (default `palette`) | Colour inputs (picked, or typed as hex) for a custom primary and second brand colour; changing one picks the `custom` choice. `ui-theme-panel` shows it under the palette. |
| `ui-dialog` | `trigger`, `triggerVariant`, `title`, `description`, `id` | A modal `<dialog>`. Escape, its ✕ or a click outside closes it. |
| `ui-alert-dialog` | same as `ui-dialog` | `role=alertdialog`; only its own buttons close it. |
| `ui-sheet` | same, plus `side` (right, left, top, bottom) | A dialog along one edge. |
| `ui-dialog-close` | `label`, `variant` | Closes the dialog it is in; its own `on.click` actions run too. |
| `ui-dialog-footer` | | A right-aligned row of buttons. |
| `ui-popover` | `trigger`, `triggerVariant`, `side` (bottom, top, right, left), `align` (center, start, end), `id` | Native popover, placed next to its trigger and flipped when there's no room. |
| `ui-dropdown-menu` | same as `ui-popover`, plus `triggerSize` | Children: `ui-menu-item` (`label`, `shortcut`, `variant`, `href`, `disabled`; choosing it runs its `on.click` and closes the menu), `ui-menu-label`, `ui-menu-separator`. Keyboard: opening focuses the first item; Up/Down, Home/End and typing move between items; Down or Up on the button opens it; Tab closes it. |
| `ui-split-button` | `label`, `variant`, `size`, `disabled`, `menuLabel` (default `More actions`), `side`, `align` (default `end`), `id` | A primary action joined to an arrow that opens a menu of secondary ones, e.g. Download PDF with Excel and CSV in the menu. Its `on.click` is the primary action; children are the menu's items, as in `ui-dropdown-menu`, keyboard included. Parts: `primary`, `trigger`. |
| `ui-tooltip` | `text`, `side`, `id` | Shown while its children are hovered or focused. CSS only. The first child (usually a button) gets `aria-describedby` pointing at the tip. |
| `ui-hover-card` | `trigger`, `href` | Children are the card, shown while the trigger is hovered or focused. CSS only. |
| `ui-toaster` | `bind`, `duration` (default 4000 ms), `max` (default 3) | Toasts at the bottom right. Setting `bind` to `{ title, description, variant, duration }` adds one to the stack. |
| `ui-sidebar-layout` + `ui-sidebar` | layout: `bind`, `collapsible` (offcanvas, icon, none), `variant` (sidebar, inset, floating), `side`, `width`; sidebar: `label` | See [Sidebar](#sidebar). |
| `ui-sidebar-header`, `ui-sidebar-content`, `ui-sidebar-footer`, `ui-sidebar-group`, `ui-sidebar-item`, `ui-sidebar-trigger` | group: `label`; item: `label`, `icon`, `href`, `active`, `badge`, `open`; trigger: `label` | The parts of a sidebar. An item with children opens a sub-menu. |
| `ui-combobox` | see [Combobox](#combobox) | A searchable select in the style of react-select: multi-select, groups, async, creatable. |
| `ui-command` | `placeholder`, `label`, `empty` (default `No results found.`), `id` | A command palette: a search box over a list of actions, filtered as you type (every word must match the label or `keywords`). Up and Down move between items, skipping disabled ones; Home and End jump while the box is empty; Enter runs the active item; Escape clears the search. Focus stays in the search box. Parts: `search`, `input`, `list`, `empty`. |
| `ui-command-dialog` | as `ui-command`, plus `trigger`, `triggerVariant`, `shortcut` (e.g. `mod+k`: ⌘K on Apple devices, Ctrl+K elsewhere), `title` (default `Command palette`) | The palette in a modal, opened by its trigger, the shortcut, or a button with `commandfor` its id. Running an item closes it, and it opens with an empty search. |
| `ui-command-group`, `ui-command-item`, `ui-command-separator` | group: `heading`; item: `label`, `keywords` (a string or a list), `icon`, `shortcut`, `href`, `disabled` | The palette's contents. An item runs its `on.click`, or follows `href`. A group hides while none of its items match, and separators hide while searching. |

| `ui-conversation` | `messages`, `typing`, `assistant`, `empty`, `label`, `height`, `maxHeight` | A chat log; see [Chat](#chat). |
| `ui-message` | `role` (assistant, user, system), `content`, `name`, `time`, `avatar`, `initials`, `replies`, `open` | One message bubble, with an optional thread. Children go in the bubble. |
| `ui-chat-input` | `messages` (required), `endpoint`, `bind`, `waiting`, `placeholder`, `label`, `suggestions`, `disabled` | The box a message is written in; sends to `endpoint` and streams the reply in. Children go in its toolbar. |
| `ui-typing-indicator` | `label` (default `Typing`) | Three bouncing dots. |
As with the built-ins, a document can override any attribute with `attrs`, any style with `style`, and inner elements with `parts`. The kit only sets defaults.

Options, items and page numbers can come from `state` as well as server data: `ui-radio-group` and `ui-toggle-group` options, `ui-breadcrumb` items, and `ui-pagination`'s `page`, `pages` and `siblings`. The server renders them for the starting state and the browser redraws them as the state changes. A breadcrumb's `items` from state must be a path, like `"{{ crumbs }}"`, so it can tell which item is last. Pagination from state adds a small behaviour that redraws its links.

`icon` on `ui-button`, `ui-badge`, `ui-alert`, `ui-sidebar-item` and `ui-command-item` takes an icon name, like `settings` or `it:database`, written in the document or coming from server data such as a list item, drawn by [irender-icon-kit](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-icon-kit/README.md) when it's registered. Otherwise, or for anything that isn't a name, it is shown as text, so an emoji or a character like `⚠` works too.

## Sidebar

A page with a navigation panel that slides away or narrows to its icons, in the style of shadcn/ui's sidebar:

```yaml
state: { sidebar: true }
root:
  type: ui-sidebar-layout
  props: { bind: sidebar, collapsible: icon, variant: inset }
  children:
    - type: ui-sidebar
      children:
        - type: ui-sidebar-header
          children: [ { type: ui-sidebar-item, props: { label: Acme Inc, icon: grid, href: / } } ]
        - type: ui-sidebar-content
          children:
            - type: ui-sidebar-group
              props: { label: Platform }
              children:
                - { type: ui-sidebar-item, props: { label: Dashboard, icon: grid, href: /, active: true } }
                - type: ui-sidebar-item
                  props: { label: Settings, icon: settings }
                  children:
                    - { type: ui-sidebar-item, props: { label: Team, href: /team } }
                    - { type: ui-sidebar-item, props: { label: Billing, href: /billing } }
        - type: ui-sidebar-footer
          children: [ { type: ui-sidebar-item, props: { label: Account, icon: user } } ]
    # Everything after the ui-sidebar is the main area.
    - type: element
      props: { tag: header }
      children: [ { type: ui-sidebar-trigger } ]
```

- **Open and closed:** `bind` holds whether the sidebar is open, and `ui-sidebar-trigger` flips it. `collapsible: offcanvas` (the default) slides the panel away, `icon` narrows it to its icons, and `none` keeps it open. Narrowed to icons, labels are hidden from sight but still read by screen readers, and sub-menus close.
- **Phones:** below 768px wide the sidebar is a sheet over the page instead. It starts hidden, the trigger opens it whatever `bind` says, and a tap on the backdrop, Escape or following one of its links closes it. While it's open the page behind is `inert` and focus is in the panel; closing it returns focus to the trigger.
- **Keyboard:** ⌘B (Ctrl+B) toggles the sidebar, or the sheet on a phone. With several layouts on a page, the first takes the shortcut.
- **Labels when collapsed:** narrowed to icons, an item shows its label beside it on hover or keyboard focus.
- **Variants:** `sidebar` puts a border between the panel and the page, `inset` makes the main area a raised panel on the sidebar's colour, and `floating` floats the panel itself.
- **Items:** a link with `href`, otherwise a button that runs its `on.click`. `active` marks the current page (`aria-current="page"`). Children make a sub-menu, a native `<details>` the item opens and closes; `open` starts it open.
- **Colour:** the panel uses `color.sidebar` when the theme has it, otherwise a step off the surface colour, in light and dark.

The [blocks](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/examples/blocks) use it: a dashboard, a sidebar that collapses to icons and one with sub-menus.

## Theme

Components read the theme's colour tokens. Tokens the default theme doesn't have fall back to values derived from `color.text` and `color.surface`, so the kit looks right with any theme, in light and dark mode:

| token | used for | fallback |
|---|---|---|
| `color.secondary` / `color.on-secondary` | secondary buttons and badges | text mixed 6% into surface / text |
| `color.accent` | hover backgrounds | text mixed 6% into surface |
| `color.subtle` | skeletons, avatars, code, table hover | text mixed 6% into surface |
| `color.destructive` / `color.on-destructive` | destructive variants | `#dc2626` / white |
| `color.ring` | focus rings | `color.muted` |
| `color.brand-2` / `color.on-brand-2` | the `brand` variant of buttons and badges: a second brand colour | `color.primary` / `color.on-primary` |

`apply_theme` merges a neutral, shadcn-style palette (zinc) with a dark mode under the document's theme. Tokens the document sets itself keep their values.

### Theme options

`apply_theme` also adds theme options, and `ui-theme-option` picks one:

```yaml
- { type: ui-theme-option, props: { option: palette, swatch: color.primary } }
- { type: ui-theme-option, props: { option: density } }
```

| option | choices | sets |
|---|---|---|
| `palette` | zinc (default), slate, stone, rose, blue, green, orange, violet, custom | every colour (neutrals) or the primary and ring (colours), each with its dark mode; custom: the colours from `ui-theme-colors` |
| `radius` | 0, 0.3, 0.5 (default), 0.75, 1.0 | `radius.sm`, `radius.md`, `radius.lg` |
| `density` | compact, default, comfortable | `space.scale`: 0.8, 1, 1.2 |
| `text-size` | small, default, large | `font.scale`: 0.9, 1, 1.125 |
| `font` | sans (default), serif, mono | `font.body` |

- **Picking:** `ui-theme-option` shows one button per choice; `swatch` names a token shown as a colour dot, or a list of them: `ui-theme-panel` shows a chart scheme's first four colours. A choice is kept in `localStorage` (`irender-theme-options`) and applied before the page shows on every page rendered with the kit, like `ui-theme-toggle`'s mode. Picking the default clears it. Pages already open follow at once, other tabs and pages in iframes included, so a picker on one page restyles the rest.
- **A Theme button:** `{ type: ui-popover, props: { trigger: Theme }, children: [ { type: ui-theme-panel } ] }` gives every option and the mode, including ones the document adds. The examples index, the blocks page and the dashboard block have one.
- **Scales:** the kit's paddings, gaps, margins and control heights are `calc(Npx * var(--space-scale, 1))`, and its font sizes `calc(Npx * var(--font-scale, 1))`, so density and text size reach every component. Use the same tokens in your own styles to follow them: `padding: "calc(16px * var(--space-scale, 1))"`.
- **Custom colours:** `ui-theme-colors` takes a primary and a second brand colour as hex (`#rgb` or `#rrggbb`, nothing else), typed or picked. They're kept in `localStorage` (`irender-theme-custom`) and set on `<html>` while the palette's `custom` choice is picked, with a hover shade, a ring and dark or light text on them (whichever reads better) derived from each. The chart kit's `custom` chart colours are built from the same two. In script: `window.__irenderTheme.custom()` and `.setCustom("primary", "#1e3a8a")`.
- **Your own:** add choices to an option (`theme.options.palette.choices.brand`) or options of your own (`theme.options.shadow`); `ui-theme-option` picks those too. The [theme block](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/examples/blocks/theme.yaml) does both.
- **In script:** `window.__irenderTheme.option("palette")` and `.setOption("palette", "rose")`; changes fire `irender:theme-option`.

## Combobox

`ui-combobox` is a searchable select modelled on [react-select](https://react-select.com/). Its behaviour (about 4 KB gzipped) is added only to pages that use it.

```yaml
- type: ui-combobox
  props:
    bind: flavours            # state key: a value, or an array with `multiple`
    multiple: true
    clearable: true
    creatable: true           # offers "Create “…”" for new text
    fixed: [chocolate]        # chips that can't be removed
    options:
      - { value: vanilla, label: Vanilla, description: Creamy and classic }
      - { label: Fruity, options: [mango, { value: lime, disabled: true }] }   # a group
```

| react-select | `ui-combobox` |
|---|---|
| `isMulti`, `isClearable`, `isSearchable`, `isDisabled`, `isLoading` | `multiple`, `clearable`, `searchable` (default true), `disabled`, `loading`. The last two can be expressions. |
| grouped options, `isOptionDisabled` | groups `{ label, options }`, `disabled` on an option |
| `getOptionValue`, `getOptionLabel` | `valueField`, `labelField`, `descriptionField`: read options from objects shaped your way, e.g. `{ href, title, summary }` |
| `AsyncSelect` `loadOptions`, `cacheOptions` | `searchUrl`: `GET <url>?q=<text>` answering an array (or `{ options }`), debounced (`debounce`, default 250 ms) after `minChars` (default 1), cached per query, stale answers dropped |
| `CreatableSelect` | `creatable`, `createText` |
| `closeMenuOnSelect`, `hideSelectedOptions` | `closeOnSelect` (default: unless `multiple`), `hideSelected` (default: with `multiple`) |
| fixed options | `fixed` |
| `name` for forms | `name`: one hidden input per value |
| `noOptionsMessage`, `loadingMessage`, `placeholder` | `noOptionsText`, `loadingText`, `placeholder` |
| options from props | `options` from data, or a state path (`"{{ cities }}"`) read live |
| `onChange` | `bind`; the element also fires a bubbling `change` event |

Matching ignores case and accents and looks at labels and values. The keyboard follows react-select:
- ↑ ↓ move through the options, skipping disabled ones.
- Home, End, Page Up and Page Down jump.
- Enter chooses. Tab chooses when you've typed something.
- Escape closes the menu, then clears the text. Inside a dialog or sheet, only an Escape with nothing left to undo closes it.
- Inside a dialog or sheet, the menu sits on top of it and flips above the field when there's no room below.
- Backspace on an empty field removes the last value.
- Space opens a non-searchable combobox.

It follows the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern (`role=combobox` / `listbox` / `option`, `aria-activedescendant`), and a live region announces result counts and choices. The menu is a popover placed under the field at its width, and flips above near the bottom of the screen.

Not replicated:
- Custom render functions (`formatOptionLabel` and friends). Options take a `description` instead.
- Chip animations.
- Values that are whole option objects: values are plain values, and their labels come from the options.
- `searchUrl` must be a path on the same site or an http(s) URL, and options loaded from it keep only the labels the API gives.

## Chat

Messages are `{ id, role, content, name, avatar, initials, time, replies }`: `role` is `assistant` (on the left; the default), `user` (on the right, in the primary colour) or `system` (a small centred note). Keep them in state and the conversation redraws as they change, keeping each message whose `id` it has seen.

```yaml
state: { messages: [], draft: "", waiting: false }
root:
  type: stack
  children:
    - type: ui-conversation
      props: { messages: "{{ messages }}", typing: "{{ waiting }}", height: 480, empty: Ask anything. }
    - type: ui-chat-input
      props: { messages: messages, bind: draft, waiting: waiting, endpoint: /api/chat, suggestions: [What can you do?] }
```

- **Sending.** Enter sends and Shift+Enter starts a new line. Sending appends `{ id, role: user, content }` to `messages`, then runs the input's `on.send` actions (the bound key still holds the text then), then clears the box. Suggestions show while `messages` is empty, and clicking one sends it.
- **Replies.** With `endpoint`, the input POSTs `{ messages }` there and adds the reply as an assistant message. The reply may be JSON (a message, `{ message }` or `{ content }`), plain text streamed as it arrives, or server-sent events whose `data` is text or JSON with `content`, `delta`, `text` or OpenAI's `choices[0].delta.content`, ending with `[DONE]`. `waiting` is true from sending until the first text arrives, which suits the conversation's `typing`. While a reply streams the send button stops it. A failed request adds a `system` message saying so.
- **Without an endpoint**, listen for `send` (an `on.send` action, or the bubbling DOM event, whose `detail` has `text` and `message`) and append the reply to the state key yourself, e.g. with `root.__irender.set`.
- **Threads.** A message's `replies` fold away under "N replies", indented with a rule; `open` unfolds them. Replies don't nest further.
- **Scrolling.** The conversation keeps to its latest message as messages arrive or stream in. Once you scroll up it stays put and shows a button that jumps back down; sending a message always does. It's a `role="log"`, so screen readers announce new messages.
- `parts.bubble`, `parts.avatar`, `parts.meta` and so on, set on the conversation, style every message it draws from `messages`.

## Overlays and ids

Dialogs, sheets, popovers and menus open from their `trigger` prop's button. To open one from your own button instead, give the overlay an `id` and put `"attrs": { "command": "show-modal", "commandfor": "<id>" }` (dialogs) or `"attrs": { "popovertarget": "<id>" }` (popovers) on the button.

Every overlay needs an element id. Without the `id` prop, one is derived from the node's place in the document. It stays unique for each item of a list rendered on the server, and inside a list the browser rebuilds from state, it ends with the item's index and follows it when the list changes. An `id` you pass can use the item too, such as `"confirm-{{ item.id }}"`. Either way, the trigger, close buttons and menu items inside follow the same id.

To show a toast, set the toaster's state key to it:

```yaml
- type: ui-button
  props: { label: Save }
  on:
    click: { action: set_state, key: toast, value: { title: Saved, description: Your changes are live. } }
- { type: ui-toaster, props: { bind: toast } }
```

The toaster adds it to a stack and clears the key, so the next one can follow. Each toast hides after its own `duration` (the toaster's, 4 seconds by default; `0` keeps it until dismissed), and at most `max` show at once, the oldest leaving first. Timers pause while the pointer is over the toasts or focus is in them. `variant: destructive` shows an error. Toasts need JavaScript: the toaster's behaviour builds them from a template the server renders, so the `toast` part still styles them.

## Browser support

The overlays rely on invoker commands (`command`/`commandfor`), `closedby`, the Popover API, CSS anchor positioning and exclusive `<details name>`. Chrome and Edge 135 and later support all of them, and the kit's browser tests run in Chrome. Check your other target browsers. Where a feature is missing:
- A popover still opens, but in the middle of the screen.
- Light dismiss falls back to Escape.
- Accordion items stop closing each other.

## Not included

Components that need focus management or keyboard navigation written in JavaScript are out of scope: date picker, data table with sorting, carousel and context menu. `ui-combobox` and `ui-dropdown-menu` have their own small behaviours.


---


# irender-chart-kit

Charts for [iRender](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/README.md) documents, drawn by [Apache ECharts](https://echarts.apache.org/) 6. Charts are fully reactive: they filter, group and drill through rows in the browser, write clicks, zooms, legends and brushes to state, and can take live data. Give `ui-chart` rows and a `type` for the common charts. For anything else ECharts can draw, give it a full ECharts `option`, or use both: the option is merged over what the shorthand builds. Charts follow the document's theme, including dark mode, and they work with [irender-ui-kit](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-ui-kit/README.md): put them in cards, drive them from its controls, and write clicks back to state.

```rust
let mut engine = irender_html::Engine::new();
irender_ui_kit::register(&mut engine.registry);      // optional
irender_chart_kit::register(&mut engine.registry);

let mut doc = irender_core::parse(src, irender_core::Format::Yaml)?;
irender_ui_kit::apply_theme(&mut doc);               // optional
irender_chart_kit::apply_theme(&mut doc);            // optional: the series colours, light and dark
let ir = engine.resolve(&doc)?;
```

From the CLI, add `--chart-kit` to `validate`, `render` or `components`:

```sh
cargo run -p irender-cli -- render examples/charts/gallery.yaml --data examples/charts/gallery.data.json \
  --ui-kit --chart-kit -o charts.html
```

[`examples/charts/gallery.yaml`](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/examples/charts/gallery.yaml) has a chart for every ECharts example category.

```yaml
- type: ui-card
  props: { title: Orders, description: This week }
  children:
    - type: ui-chart
      props: { type: bar, data: "{{ week }}", x: day, y: [orders, returns], stack: true }
```

## Loading ECharts

ECharts is 1.1 MB (about 360 KB gzipped), so it isn't inlined. Pages with a chart load it once from [`ChartKit::src`](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-chart-kit/src/lib.rs), and pages without one don't load it at all. The default is jsDelivr, pinned to `echarts@6.1.0`. To serve your own copy, or to use the SVG renderer:

```rust
irender_chart_kit::register_with(&mut engine.registry, irender_chart_kit::ChartKit {
    src: "/static/echarts.min.js".into(),
    renderer: irender_chart_kit::Renderer::Svg,
});
```

The kit's own script is about 10 KB gzipped and is added once per page. If the host page loads ECharts itself (`window.echarts`), the kit uses that copy. Extensions such as echarts-gl or custom series registered on it work too.

## `ui-chart`

| prop | |
|---|---|
| `type` | The series the shorthand builds (see below). Leave it out to use `option` alone. |
| `data` | Rows: objects (`{ day: Mon, orders: 120 }`) or arrays (`[Mon, 120]`, with `x`/`y` as column numbers). Plain numbers are fine too; their position is the category. |
| `x` | The category or name field. Default: the first field. |
| `y` | Value field(s): `orders`, `[orders, returns]`, or `{ field, name, …series options }` per series. Default: every other numeric field. |
| `value` | A third field: the heatmap's cell value or a scatter point's size. |
| `links` | `{ source, target, value }` for `sankey`, `graph` and `chord`. Nodes are taken from `data`, or from the links. |
| `filter`, `aggregate`, `series`, `sort`, `limit` | Shape the rows before drawing; see [Filters and grouping](#filters-and-grouping). |
| `drill` | Fields to click down through, e.g. `[region, country, city]`; see [Drill-downs](#drill-downs). |
| `xType` | `category`, `time`, `value` or `log`. Default: `time` when every x is a date or epoch milliseconds, on lines and points. |
| `zoom` | Zoom along the category or time axis: `inside` (wheel and drag), `slider`, or `both` (`true`). |
| `brush` | Drag to select points: `rect` (`true`), `polygon`, `lineX` or `lineY`. |
| `live` | Live data for this chart; see [Live data](#live-data). |
| `option` | An [ECharts option](https://echarts.apache.org/en/option.html), merged over the shorthand's. Arrays of objects (`series`, `xAxis`, …) merge by position, like ECharts' own merge. Data arrays are replaced. |
| `stack`, `smooth`, `horizontal`, `labels` | Shorthand switches. |
| `legend`, `tooltip` | On or off. Default: a legend with two or more series, and a tooltip always. |
| `height` | Number (px) or CSS length. Default 320. The width is the container's. |
| `loading` | Shows the loading mask, e.g. `{{ fetching }}`. |
| `bind`, `bindRow`, `bindZoom`, `bindLegend`, `bindBrush`, `bindDrill` | State keys for what people do with the chart; see [Interactions as state](#interactions-as-state). |
| `maps` | GeoJSON maps to register before drawing: `{ world: /geo/world.json }`. The URLs are checked against the policy. |
| `group` | Charts in one group share tooltips and zoom (`echarts.connect`). |
| `renderer` | `canvas` or `svg`, for this chart. |
| `title` | Accessible name. ECharts' own description of the data follows it. |

`ui-sparkline` is a small chart with no axes, legend or padding, for stat cards and table cells. It takes `data` (numbers, or rows with `y`), `type` (`area`, `line` or `bar`), `width`, `height` (default 40), `tooltip`, `option` and `live`.

### Shorthand types

| `type` | `data` | `x` / `y` |
|---|---|---|
| `line`, `area`, `bar`, `pictorialBar` | rows | category / value field(s) |
| `scatter`, `effectScatter` | rows | x / y field(s); `value` sizes the points |
| `candlestick` | rows | date / `[open, close, low, high]`, found by name when the fields are called that |
| `boxplot` | rows | group / one field of raw samples (the quartiles are computed), or five fields: min, Q1, median, Q3, max |
| `pie`, `donut`, `funnel` | rows | name / value field |
| `radar` | rows: one polygon each | name / one field per axis |
| `heatmap` | rows | column / row field; `value` colours the cell |
| `gauge` | a number, `{ name, value }`, one object with the value in `y` (e.g. a live reading), or rows | name / value |
| `tree` | `{ name, children }` | |
| `treemap`, `sunburst` | `[{ name, value, children }]` | |
| `sankey`, `graph`, `chord` | nodes (optional; a `category` field colours graph nodes) plus `links` | |
| `themeRiver` | rows | date / one stream per field |
| `parallel` | rows: one line each | / one axis per field; text fields become category axes |

Everything else goes in `option`: maps and `lines`, `custom` series, calendars, the `matrix` coordinate system, polar charts, `dataset` with transforms, `dataZoom`, `visualMap`, `markLine`, `graphic`, and 3D with echarts-gl. The gallery shows a calendar, polar bars and a sorted dataset written that way.

## State

Every prop can use state, so a chart redraws when the state it reads changes. That includes `{{ }}` anywhere inside `option`:

```yaml
- { type: ui-toggle-group, props: { bind: kind, options: [bar, line, area] } }
- type: ui-chart
  props:
    type: "{{ kind }}"
    data: "{{ results }}"            # e.g. filled by a `submit` with `into: results`
    loading: "{{ fetching }}"
    option: { title: { text: "{{ heading }}" } }
```

Server data is filled in at render time, and only the parts that read state are evaluated in the browser. A redraw that keeps the type and the components merges into the chart on screen, so values animate. A redraw that changes them starts over.

Clicks go the other way. Bind the chart, then load details for what was clicked:

```yaml
- type: ui-chart
  props: { type: bar, data: "{{ regions }}", bind: region }
  on:
    change: { action: submit, method: GET, endpoint: "/api/regions/{{ region }}", into: regionSales }
- { type: ui-chart, props: { type: donut, data: "{{ regionSales }}" } }
```

## Filters and grouping

Rows go through these steps, in order, before they are drawn. Each prop can read state, so a control bound to a state key filters every chart that uses it.

1. **`drill`**: the current level's rows (see below).
2. **`filter`**: an object of field → condition. A row is kept when every condition holds:

   | condition | keeps rows whose field… |
   |---|---|
   | `Europe`, `3` | equals it. Text and numbers compare loosely, so `"3"` from a form control matches `3`. |
   | `[Laptops, Phones]` | is one of them. A list of rows compares the same field of each, so `"{{ picked }}"` from `bindBrush` works. |
   | `{ from, to }` | is in the range, ends included. Dates compare as dates, numbers as numbers. This is the shape `bindZoom` writes. |
   | `{ gt, gte, lt, lte }` | compares that way. |
   | `{ contains: text }` | contains the text, ignoring case and accents. |
   | `{ not: … }` | fails the inner condition. |
   | a row, e.g. from `bindRow` | equals that row's same field. |

   Blank conditions (null, `""`, `[]`, or `{ from: null }`) keep every row. A filter bound to an empty control shows everything rather than nothing.
3. **`aggregate`**: `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max` or `count`. Groups rows by `x`, and by `series` if set, and aggregates the `y` fields. Each group also gets a `count`. With `count`, `y` defaults to it.
4. **`sort`**: a field, `-field` for descending, `{ field, order }`, or a list of these.
5. **`limit`**: the first N rows.

`series: product` turns long-format rows (`{ month, product, amount }`) into one series per product, aligned on the categories.

```yaml
- type: ui-chart
  props:
    type: bar
    data: "{{ orders }}"          # every order, once, in state
    x: city
    y: amount
    aggregate: sum
    sort: -amount
    limit: 5
    filter: { product: "{{ products }}", date: "{{ range }}", region: "{{ region }}", channel: { not: Store } }
```

## Drill-downs

`drill` lists the fields to click down through. The chart starts grouped by the first field (summed unless `aggregate` says otherwise). Clicking a bar or slice filters to it and groups by the next field. A trail at the top left (`‹ All › Europe`) goes back up a level. The marks morph between levels.

```yaml
- type: ui-chart
  props: { type: bar, data: "{{ orders }}", drill: [region, country, city], y: amount, sort: -amount, bindDrill: geoPath }
- { type: ui-button, props: { label: Top }, on: { click: { action: set_state, key: geoPath, value: [] } } }
```

`bindDrill` keeps the path (`[Europe, Germany]`) in state, both ways. Other kinds of drill-down need no special support:
- **Into another chart:** `bind` the clicked item, and `filter` the other chart by it.
- **Into the server:** react to `on: { change: … }` with a `submit` that fetches details `into` state.
- **To another page:** `navigate` from `on.change`.
- **Within a hierarchy:** `treemap` and `sunburst` zoom into a node when it's clicked.

## Interactions as state

| prop | state holds | from state |
|---|---|---|
| `bind` | the clicked item's name (its x, or value). Clicking it again clears it, so a click works as a toggled filter. | selects (highlights) that item |
| `bindRow` | the clicked item's row (after grouping) | |
| `bindZoom` | the zoom window as `{ from, to }` in axis values (categories, dates in the data's own format, or numbers), or null when it shows everything | zooms there; null zooms out |
| `bindLegend` | the names of the visible series (or slices) | shows only those; null shows all |
| `bindBrush` | the rows inside the brushed area | `[]` clears the brush |
| `bindDrill` | the drill path | goes to that level |

Each interaction also fires a bubbling DOM event for `on:` actions: `change` (a click), `drill`, `zoom`, `legend` and `brush`. `bindZoom` works without `zoom` too: the window then moves only from state. Writing the zoom state on one chart and a `filter: { date: "{{ range }}" }` on others gives the classic overview-and-detail dashboard. The gallery's "Drill-downs, filters and live data" section wires all of these together.

## Live data

A chart's `live` prop, or the `ui-live-data` component, keeps data coming in:

```yaml
# One source in state, for any number of components:
- type: ui-live-data
  props: { url: /api/metrics, every: 1000, mode: append, window: 300, key: time,
           into: metrics, status: feedStatus, paused: "{{ !liveOn }}", params: { host: "{{ host }}" } }
- { type: ui-chart, props: { type: line, data: "{{ metrics }}", x: time, y: [cpu, memory], zoom: inside } }
- { type: ui-badge, props: { text: "{{ feedStatus }}" } }

# Or straight into one chart:
- type: ui-chart
  props: { type: scatter, x: time, y: amount, xType: time,
           live: { url: /api/orders/stream, stream: true, mode: append, window: 100, key: id } }
```

| setting | |
|---|---|
| `url` | Polled with GET. With `stream: true` it is read as server-sent events, and `ws://` / `wss://` URLs are WebSockets. It may use state. Script URLs are refused, and a URL known on the server must pass the policy. |
| `every` | Milliseconds between polls (default 5000, at least 250). The next poll waits for the previous response, and polling waits while the tab is hidden. |
| `mode` | `replace` (default): each message is the data. `append`: messages (a row or a list of rows) are added. |
| `window` | With `append`, keep the last N rows (default 500). |
| `key` | With `append`, a row with the same value in this field replaces the old one. Use it for upserts, or to make a re-sent row harmless. |
| `pick` | A path to the data inside each message, e.g. `data.items`. |
| `params` | Query parameters. Blank ones are left out, so filters can go to the server: `{ from: "{{ range.from }}" }`. A change reconnects at once. |
| `paused` | Disconnects while true. |
| `into` | A state key that gets the data (required on `ui-live-data`). On a chart it's optional, and shares the chart's data. |
| `status` | A state key set to `connecting`, `live`, `paused` or `error`. The element also carries `data-live` (chart) or `data-status`. |

WebSockets reconnect with backoff up to 30 s, and EventSource reconnects by itself. Live data goes through the same filters, grouping and drill as any other data, and when the type and components stay the same the chart animates new points in. For the gallery's live charts, serve the examples with `python3 examples/serve.py`, which adds a polled metrics endpoint and an order stream.

## Functions

ECharts takes functions in some places: formatters, `renderItem` for custom series, symbol sizes. A document is JSON, so it names a function, and the host page provides it:

```yaml
option: { yAxis: { axisLabel: { formatter: { $fn: money } } } }
```

```html
<script>window.irenderChartFunctions = { money: (v) => "$" + v.toLocaleString() };</script>
```

Functions are looked up whenever the chart draws, so define them in an ordinary script on the page. A document can only use the functions the host defines. Many formatters don't need a function at all: ECharts' string templates such as `"{b}: {c}"` work as they are.

## Theme

The kit reads the page's CSS tokens and turns them into an ECharts theme:
- Text uses `color.text` and `color.muted`.
- Axis and grid lines use `color.border`.
- Tooltips, and the gaps between slices and cells, use `color.surface`.
- Series colours come from `color.chart-1` … `color.chart-8`.

Values such as `color-mix()` are resolved by the browser first. A missing token falls back to the element's own colours, so charts look right without any theme.

`apply_theme` adds eight series colours. Each has its own step for dark mode, and they're in an order where neighbouring colours stay distinct for colour-blind readers. The heatmap's sequential scale runs from `chart-1` down into the surface colour. When the colour scheme changes, or a theme attribute (`class`, `style`, `data-theme`) changes on `<html>` or `<body>`, every chart restyles itself, as it does when a theme option is picked.

`apply_theme` also adds a `chart` theme option, the colour scheme: Default (the eight hues above), Blue, Rose, Green, Orange and Violet (shades of one colour, to match the UI kit's palettes) Mono, and Custom (eight colours built from the custom primary and second brand colour picked with irender-ui-kit's `ui-theme-colors`). Pick it with irender-ui-kit's `{ type: ui-theme-option, props: { option: chart, swatch: color.chart-1 } }`, or add schemes of your own under `theme.options.chart.choices`.

Defaults follow common charting practice:
- 2 px lines.
- Bars rounded at the data end.
- Value axes without an axis line, and faint grid lines.
- Category labels shown wherever they fit.
- A tooltip on every chart.
- No animation for people who ask their system for reduced motion.

ECharts' `aria` description is on, so screen readers get a summary of the data.

## Lifecycle

- A chart starts once it has a size, so charts in closed tabs, dialogs and `if`s start when they're shown.
- It follows its container's size.
- It is disposed of when it leaves the page (an `if` that hides it, a list rebuilt from state), and drawn again if it comes back.

## Untrusted documents

ECharts tooltips are HTML. With [`Engine::untrusted`](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-html/src/lib.rs) (any policy that blocks event attributes or unsafe URLs):
- Tooltip `formatter` strings are escaped. Line breaks (`<br>`) still work.
- `extraCssText` is dropped.
- `title.link` must not be a `javascript:`, `vbscript:` or `data:` URL.
- Map URLs are checked against the policy.

Data values in tooltips are escaped by ECharts itself. Functions can only be ones the host defines.

## Tests

```sh
cargo test -p irender-chart-kit                                   # rendering and config
cargo test -p irender-chart-kit --test browser -- --ignored       # in Chrome: every type, drill, filters, zoom, legend, brush, live data, theme, lifecycle
ECHARTS=path/to/echarts.min.js cargo test -p irender-chart-kit --test browser -- --ignored   # offline
```


---


# irender-flow-kit

Node-and-edge diagrams for [iRender](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/README.md) documents: flowcharts, workflows and ER diagrams. `ui-flow` reads nodes and edges in [React Flow](https://reactflow.dev/)'s JSON shape, so a graph React Flow saved renders as it is. Every node type is a template you write as an ordinary iRender tree, so a node can hold any component, including [irender-ui-kit](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-ui-kit/README.md)'s, icons and sparklines. The kit's script handles pan and zoom, automatic layout, edge routing, selection, dragging, connecting, deleting, a palette, containers, copy and paste, undo, search and the minimap. It is about 26 KB gzipped (unminified), needs no other library, and is added once per page that has a flow.

```rust
let mut engine = irender_html::Engine::new();
irender_ui_kit::register(&mut engine.registry);      // optional
irender_flow_kit::register(&mut engine.registry);
```

From the CLI, add `--flow-kit` to `validate`, `render` or `components`:

```sh
cargo run -p irender-cli -- render examples/flow/gallery.yaml --data examples/flow/gallery.data.json \
  --ui-kit --flow-kit -o flow.html
```

## React Flow JSON as it is

```yaml
- type: ui-flow
  props: { nodes: "{{ graph.nodes }}", edges: "{{ graph.edges }}", height: 400 }
```

Without templates, every node is drawn by the default node, which shows `data.label` with a target port and a source port. `input` nodes have no target port and `output` nodes no source port, as in React Flow.

The kit reads these fields:

- **Nodes:** `id`, `type`, `position`, `data`, `parentId` (the position is relative to the parent), `hidden`, `className`, `style`, and `width` / `height` (used as minimum sizes).
- **Edges:** `id`, `source`, `target`, `sourceHandle`, `targetHandle`, `type`, `label`, `animated`, `markerEnd` / `markerStart` (`arrow`, `arrowclosed`, or `{ type }`), `className`, `style` (stroke properties) and `hidden`.

Other fields are kept and ignored.

React Flow's own edge types pick the path: `default` and `simplebezier` draw a bezier, and `straight`, `step` and `smoothstep` draw those shapes.

## Node types are templates

```yaml
- type: ui-flow
  props: { nodes: "{{ wf.nodes }}", edges: "{{ wf.edges }}", layout: layered }
  children:
    - type: ui-flow-node
      props: { type: if }
      children:
        - { type: ui-badge, props: { text: If } }
        - { type: text, props: { value: "{{ node.data.label }}" } }
        - { type: ui-flow-port, props: { type: target } }
        - { type: ui-flow-port, props: { id: "true", side: right } }
        - { type: ui-flow-port, props: { id: "false", side: bottom } }
    - type: ui-flow-node            # one port per case, each on its own row
      props: { type: switch }
      children:
        - type: list
          props: { items: "{{ node.data.cases }}", as: c }
          children:
            - type: element
              style: { position: relative, padding: 4px 12px }
              children:
                - { type: text, props: { value: "{{ c.label }}" } }
                - { type: ui-flow-port, props: { id: "{{ c.handle }}", side: right } }
```

How templates work:

- **Which template a node gets:** a `ui-flow-node` draws every node whose `type` matches its own. One without a `type` (or with `type: default`) draws the rest.
- **What a template can read:** inside a template, `node` is the node and `nodeIndex` is its position in the array. Templates can also read state and server data, like any other part of the document.
- **Styling:** the template's `style`, `class`, `attrs` and `on` apply to the node's box. `variant: card` (the default) adds a border, background and padding; `variant: plain` leaves all of that to you.
- **State styling:** nodes carry attributes you can style with `"&[data-selected]": { … }`:

  | Attribute | When |
  |---|---|
  | `data-selected` | The node is selected |
  | `data-dimmed` | `highlight` or `search` dims it |
  | `data-match` | `search` matches it |
  | `data-active` | It is the current match |
  | `data-drop-target` | It is the container a dragged node would drop into |

`ui-flow-port` marks where edges attach:

| prop | |
|---|---|
| `id` | Matched against an edge's `sourceHandle` / `targetHandle`. It can use the node, e.g. `{{ c.handle }}`. An edge with no handle uses the first port of the right type. |
| `type` | `source` (default) or `target`. |
| `side` | `left`, `right`, `top` or `bottom`. Leave it out and it follows the flow's `direction`: for `LR`, targets go on the left and sources on the right. |
| `offset` | How far along the side, e.g. `30%` or `24` (px). Leave it out and ports sharing a side of the node are spread evenly. |

A port is placed on the side of its nearest positioned ancestor. Usually that's the node itself, even through wrappers like a `list`'s, and the port's edges start at the node's border. A port inside an element with `position: relative`, such as a table row, sits on that element instead. That's how one node can have a port per row.

For a number of ports, such as a merge's inputs, list over `range`:

```yaml
- type: list
  props: { items: "{{ range(node.data.inputCount) }}", as: i }
  children: [{ type: ui-flow-port, props: { id: "input-{{ i }}", type: target } }]
```

### Shapes

```yaml
- type: ui-flow-node
  props: { type: if, shape: diamond }          # or "{{ node.data.shape }}"
  style: { width: 170, height: 96 }
  parts: { shape: { style: { fill: "#fff1f2", stroke: "#f43f5e" } } }
  children:
    - { type: text, props: { value: "{{ node.data.label }}" } }
    - { type: ui-flow-port, props: { type: target } }        # the left tip
    - { type: ui-flow-port, props: { id: "true" } }           # the right tip
    - { type: ui-flow-port, props: { id: "false", side: bottom } }
```

`shape` draws the node's outline behind its content.

- **Available shapes:** `rect`, `rounded`, `pill`, `circle`, `ellipse`, `diamond`, `hexagon`, `parallelogram`, `triangle` and `cylinder`. `polygon` with `points` (corners in percent of the box, e.g. `0,20 50,0 100,20 85,100 15,100`) covers anything else.
- **Shape from data:** it can come from the node, e.g. `"{{ node.data.shape || 'rect' }}"`, and a node redraws when its shape changes.
- **Drawing:**
  - The outline is drawn at the node's size in pixels, so pill ends and cylinder rims don't stretch.
  - With `variant: card`, the box itself has no border or background, and the content is centred.
  - Style the outline through `parts.shape`, with `fill`, `stroke` and `stroke-width`.
- **Ports:** a port on the node sits on the outline: a diamond's left port is its left tip, and one `offset` 25% down its left side lies on the slanted edge.
- **Edges:** floating edges meet the outline too, not the box.
- **State:** selection and keyboard focus show on the outline rather than as a box around the node.
- **Minimap:** it draws the shapes.

### Containers

```yaml
- type: ui-flow-node
  props: { type: loop, variant: plain, container: true, resizable: true, minWidth: 260, minHeight: 140 }
  style: { border: 1.5px dashed $color.border, border-radius: 12 }
  children:
    - { type: text, props: { value: "{{ node.data.label }}" } }
    - { type: ui-flow-port, props: { type: target } }
    - { type: ui-flow-port, props: { id: done } }
    - type: element                     # inside, top left, facing in
      style: { position: absolute, left: 12, top: 44, width: 0, height: 0 }
      children: [{ type: ui-flow-port, props: { id: start, scope: children, side: right, offset: 0 } }]
```

- **Nesting:** a node whose `parentId` names a `container` sits inside it. Its `position` is relative to the container's corner, and it moves with the container. The container is drawn under the nodes inside it, and edges between those nodes are drawn above it.
- **Size:** a container, or any `resizable` node, is exactly its JSON `width` × `height`. Other nodes use those as minimum sizes and grow with their content.
- **Moving in and out:** while dragging (when `draggable`), the innermost container under the node's centre is marked `data-drop-target`. Dropping the node there moves it inside: it keeps its place on screen, and its `parentId` and relative `position` are written. Dragging it out of its container moves it back out. The nodes array is kept with parents before their children, as React Flow requires.
- **Edges across containers:** with `connect.sameParent`, an edge that would cross from one container to another isn't allowed. One that a move leaves crossing is removed.
- **`scope: children`:** a port with this connects only to nodes inside its own node, whatever `sameParent` says. This is the loop's start port.
- **Resizing:** `resizable` adds a handle in the bottom-right corner, shown on hover and selection. Dragging it writes `width` and `height`, no smaller than `minWidth` / `minHeight`.

## Edge types

```yaml
- type: ui-flow-edge
  props: { marker: arrowclosed }                 # every edge without a template of its own
- type: ui-flow-edge
  props: { type: retry, path: step, marker: arrowclosed }
  style: { stroke: "#dc2626", stroke-dasharray: "4 3" }
  parts: { label: { style: { color: "#dc2626" } } }
  children:                                       # the label: any tree, with `edge` in scope
    - { type: ui-button, props: { label: Retry, size: sm }, on: { click: { action: call, name: retry, args: { id: "{{ edge.id }}" } } } }
```

Edge templates have these props:

- **`path`:** `bezier`, `straight`, `step` or `smoothstep`.
- **`marker` / `markerStart`:** `none`, `arrow` or `arrowclosed`.
- **`animated`:** moving dashes.
- **`floating`:** the edge attaches to the two boxes' borders, facing each other, instead of to ports. This suits ER diagrams. A floating edge from a node to itself, such as a `parent_id`, is drawn as a loop off its top-right corner.

A template's `style` styles the path. Its children are the label, which sits at the middle of the path. Without children, the label is `edge.label`.

## `ui-flow`

| prop | |
|---|---|
| `nodes`, `edges` | Arrays in React Flow's shape. From state, the browser rebuilds them whenever they change, keyed by id: a node that stays keeps its DOM, including input values and the state of the components inside it. |
| `layout` | `layered` places the top-level nodes in ranks along `direction`, ignoring their positions; the layout also updates when the nodes or their sizes change. Groups of nodes that don't connect to each other are packed into rows, largest first. Default: use `position`. |
| `direction` | `LR` (default), `TB`, `RL` or `BT`. |
| `nodeGap`, `rankGap` | Layout spacing (40, 80). |
| `nodeOrigin` | Which point of the node `position` names: `[0, 0]` top left (default), `[0.5, 0]` top centre, … |
| `edgePath` | The path for edges whose type and template don't choose one (default `bezier`). |
| `fit`, `fitPadding` | Fit the view to the nodes when they first appear (default true, padding 0.1). Fitting never zooms in past 1. |
| `viewport` | `{ x, y, zoom }` to start at when `fit` is false. React Flow saves this with `toObject()`. |
| `center` | A node id; the view pans to that node whenever this changes. |
| `highlight` | `neighbors`: while a node is selected, everything not connected to it is dimmed. |
| `selectable`, `pan`, `zoom` | Defaults: all true. |
| `editable` | Turns on `draggable`, `connectable` and `deletable` together. Each can still be set on its own. See [Editing](#editing). |
| `draggable`, `connectable`, `deletable` | Default: `editable`. |
| `connect` | Connection rules; see [Editing](#editing). |
| `newEdge` | Fields every new edge starts with, e.g. `{ type: smoothstep, markerEnd: arrowclosed }`. |
| `newNode` | A node (`{ type, data }`) made where a connection is dropped on empty canvas, and joined to it. |
| `confirmDelete` | The element id of a dialog to open before deleting. |
| `wheel` | `zoom` (default) or `pan`, which leaves zooming to Ctrl/⌘ + wheel. |
| `minZoom`, `maxZoom` | 0.1 and 2. |
| `background` | `dots` (default), `lines` or `none`. |
| `controls`, `minimap` | The zoom/fit buttons (default on) and an overview that pans the view when clicked or dragged (default off). Style them through `parts`. |
| `height` | Default 480. The width is the container's. |
| `title` | Accessible name. |
| `bind` | State key with the selected node's id (the last one selected), or null. It works in both directions. |
| `bindNode` | State key with the selected node itself (`id`, `type`, `data`, …), or null, kept up to date: for a side panel that shows it, with `flow.update` to change it. |
| `bindSelection` | State key with every selected node and edge, `{ nodes: [ids], edges: [ids] }`, in both directions. |
| `bindNodes` | State key that gets the nodes array after a drag, an added node or a deletion. Point `nodes` at the same key to keep them in sync. |
| `bindEdges` | The same for edges, after a connection or a deletion. |
| `bindDelete` | With `confirmDelete`: what would be deleted, `{ nodes, edges }`, while the dialog is open. Null otherwise. |
| `bindViewport` | State key kept in sync with `{ x, y, zoom }`. |
| `nodeStyles` | Apply each node's saved `style` and `className` (default true). Turn it off when the template works the look out from `data`, as the process canvas does from `step_color`, so changing the data changes the look. |
| `filter` | Node ids to show. The nodes they connect to stay as context, marked `data-neighbor` (dashed); everything else is hidden. Empty or null shows all. The ER example drives it from a multi-select. |
| `filterNeighbors` | With `filter`, keep the neighbours (default true). |
| `search` | Text to find in the nodes' text and ids, ignoring case and accents. Matches get `data-match`; everything else is dimmed. The view pans to the first match. |
| `bindMatches` | State key with the ids `search` matches. |
| `bindHistory` | State key with how many edits can be undone and redone, `{ undo, redo }`, e.g. to disable buttons. |

Every prop except `background`, `controls`, `minimap`, `height` and `title` can use state.

The flow fires these events, which you can handle in `on`. Each fires after its bound state is written, so actions can read it:

- **`nodeselect`:** the selection changed.
- **`nodeopen`:** on a double-click, or Enter on a node that is already selected.
- **`nodemove`:** a node was dragged.
- **`connect`:** an edge was added.
- **`nodeadd`:** a node was added.
- **`noderesize`:** a node was resized.
- **`nodeupdate`:** `flow.update` changed a node's data.
- **`deleterequest`:** a deletion is waiting for its dialog.
- **`delete`:** nodes or edges were deleted.

`ui-flow-panel` children (`position`: `top-left` … `bottom-right`) float above the flow without panning or zooming, so toolbars and legends go there.

## Editing

```yaml
- type: ui-flow
  attrs: { id: wf }
  props:
    nodes: "{{ wf.nodes }}"
    edges: "{{ wf.edges }}"
    bindNodes: wf.nodes          # edits are written here …
    bindEdges: wf.edges          # … and here
    editable: true
    connect: { sameParent: true, pairs: [{ source: trigger, target: step }, { source: step }] }
    newEdge: { type: smoothstep }
    newNode: { type: step, data: { label: New step } }
    confirmDelete: confirm-delete
    bindDelete: doomed
- type: ui-flow-item             # a palette entry: drag it onto the flow, or click it
  props: { flow: wf, node: { type: step, data: { label: New step } } }
  children: [{ type: ui-badge, props: { text: Step } }]
```

The kit makes every edit itself and writes the result to `bindNodes` / `bindEdges`; expressions can't build arrays. Point `nodes` and `edges` at the same keys and the flow follows.

- **Connecting:** drag from a port to a port of the other type, starting at either end. Dropping on a node's body joins the first of its ports that the rules allow. While dragging, the port under the pointer turns green or red. Dropping on empty canvas makes a `newNode` there and joins it.
- **Connection rules:** a connection is refused when any rule says no.

  | Rule | What it refuses |
  |---|---|
  | `connect.self` | A node joined to itself, unless set |
  | `connect.unique` | A second edge between the same two ports (set it to false to allow one) |
  | `connect.sameParent` | Two nodes with different parents |
  | `connect.pairs` | Any pair of node types not in this allow-list of `{ source, target }` (either may be left out) |
  | A port's `accepts` | Node types not in this list at the other end |
  | A port's `max` | More edges than this at the port |
  | A port's `connectable: false` | Any new connection at the port |
  | A port's `scope: children` | A node outside the port's own node (see [Containers](#containers)) |

  A port's rules can use state.
- **Selecting:**
  - Click a node or an edge to select it. Shift, ⌘ or Ctrl + click adds it to the selection.
  - Shift + drag on the background selects every node inside the box.
  - ⌘/Ctrl + A selects all nodes.
  - Dragging a selected node moves the whole selection.
- **Deleting:** Delete or Backspace removes the selection. A deleted node's edges and child nodes go with it. With `confirmDelete`, the flow writes what would go to `bindDelete` and opens that dialog instead. The dialog's buttons answer it with `flow.delete` or `flow.cancel`:

  ```yaml
  - type: ui-alert-dialog
    props: { id: confirm-delete, title: Delete?, description: "{{ doomed.nodes.length }} node(s) and {{ doomed.edges.length }} edge(s)" }
    children:
      - type: ui-dialog-footer
        children:
          - { type: ui-dialog-close, props: { label: Cancel, variant: outline }, on: { click: { action: call, name: flow.cancel, args: { flow: wf } } } }
          - { type: ui-dialog-close, props: { label: Delete, variant: destructive }, on: { click: { action: call, name: flow.delete, args: { flow: wf } } } }
  ```
- **Adding:** `ui-flow-item` takes a `node` (`{ type, data }`, and an `id` to keep). Dragging it onto the flow adds the node where it's dropped; clicking it, or pressing Enter or Space, adds it in the middle of the view. Its `flow` is the flow's element id. It can be left out when the item is inside the flow, or the page has one flow. New ids are the type in snake_case plus a number, such as `step_3` or `service_call_1`.

### Commands

A `call` whose name starts with `flow.` is a command to the flow:

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `flow.fit`, `flow.zoomin`, `flow.zoomout` | Fit or zoom the view |
| `flow.delete` | Answers a pending `confirmDelete`, or deletes the selection |
| `flow.cancel` | Drops a pending deletion |
| `flow.add` | Adds `args.node` in the middle of the view, or at `args.position` |
| `flow.select` | Selects `args.id`, or clears the selection when it's null |
| `flow.center` | Pans to `args.id` |
| `flow.relayout` | Clears dragged positions and lays the nodes out again |
| `flow.undo`, `flow.redo` | Steps back or forward through the flow's own edits |
| `flow.copy`, `flow.cut`, `flow.paste` | The clipboard, as with the keys |
| `flow.next`, `flow.prev` | Steps through `search`'s matches, panning to each |
| `flow.update` | Merges the call's other args into a node's `data`: the node `args.id` names, or the selected one. One undo step. With `bindNode`, this is a side form: fields bound to state, and an Apply button that sends them |
| `flow.fullscreen` | Shows the flow fullscreen, or leaves fullscreen, fitting the view to the new size |

Commands from inside the flow, such as a panel button, a node, or a dialog in either, reach it directly. From elsewhere, add `args.flow` with the flow's element id; without it, a command reaches the page's only flow.

### Copy, paste and undo

- **Copy and cut:** ⌘/Ctrl + C copies the selection, with everything inside any selected container and the edges between the copied nodes. Cut copies, then deletes.
- **Paste:** ⌘/Ctrl + V adds a copy with new ids, each named after its original (`check_stock` becomes `check_stock_1`), and selects it. It lands at the pointer when the pointer is over the flow; otherwise it lands a step down and right of the original. Copies keep their container when it still exists. The clipboard is shared by the page's flows, so you can copy between them. The copies' `data` is unchanged, so if it holds ids of its own, have the host app remap them (e.g. `on: { nodeadd: { action: call, … } }`).
- **Undo:** every edit the flow makes is one undo step: a drag, connection, deletion, resize, added node or paste. Undo (⌘/Ctrl + Z, or `flow.undo`) puts both arrays back as they were. Changes made to the state outside the flow aren't recorded. The flow keeps the last 100 steps.

## Mouse, touch and keyboard

| Input | What it does |
|---|---|
| Drag the background | Pans the view |
| Wheel or pinch | Zooms |
| Click a node or edge | Selects it (Shift adds to the selection) |
| Click the background | Clears the selection |
| Shift + drag the background | Box selection |
| Drag a node | Moves it, with the rest of the selection, when `draggable` is on |
| Drag from a port | Connects, when `connectable` is on |
| Drag a node onto a container | Moves it inside; dragging it out moves it out |
| Drag a node's corner handle | Resizes it, when it is `resizable` |

Controls inside nodes (buttons, inputs, links) work as usual and don't start a drag. Add `data-flow-nodrag` to any other element that should behave the same way.

The flow and its nodes are focusable:

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| Tab | Moves focus to the flow and its nodes |
| Enter / Space | Selects the focused node |
| Escape | Cancels a connection, or clears the selection |
| Delete / Backspace | Deletes the selection, when `deletable` is on |
| ⌘/Ctrl + Z, ⌘/Ctrl + Shift + Z (or Ctrl + Y) | Undo, redo |
| ⌘/Ctrl + C, X, V | Copy, cut, paste |
| ⌘/Ctrl + A | Selects all nodes |
| `+` / `-` | Zoom |
| Arrows | Pan, or move the selection when a node has focus and `draggable` is on (Shift for bigger steps) |

## Safety

The JSON's `style` objects are applied one property at a time, so a value can't escape its property. In documents rendered with `Engine::untrusted()`, values containing `url(` are dropped as well. `className` only adds classes. Labels are text, unless a template renders them.

## Examples

- [`examples/flow/gallery.yaml`](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/examples/flow/gallery.yaml):
  - plain React Flow JSON
  - an editable workflow with a palette
  - containers with undo and search
  - an ER diagram from server data
- [`examples/flow/process.yaml`](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/examples/flow/process.yaml) loads a workflow canvas in the format client-ui-next's process canvas saves ([`process-canvas.json`](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/examples/flow/process-canvas.json), made up):
  - **Milestones:** coloured from their `step_color` (with `nodeStyles: false`), with status icons.
  - **Editing:** a palette, a side form for the selected milestone (`bindNode` and `flow.update`), cut, copy and paste, undo, and a confirmation before deleting.
  - **Edges:** the app's CSS variables, such as `--foreground` in its saved edge styles, are set on the flow from the theme.
- [`examples/flow/er.yaml`](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/examples/flow/er.yaml) draws a package (the JSON files the builder edits) as an ER diagram, after the builder's own:
  - **Tables:** key and constraint badges, `<details>` to collapse each one, and placeholders for tables in other packages.
  - **Toolbar:** a filter that keeps neighbours, keys only, LR/TB and fullscreen.
  - **Data:** the [`package_er`](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-flow-kit/examples/package_er.rs) example turns the package into nodes and edges. That's host code, the same work the builder does in `buildGraph`:

    ```sh
    cargo run -p irender-flow-kit --example package_er -- path/to/package > er.data.json
    cargo run -p irender-cli -- render examples/flow/er.yaml --data er.data.json --ui-kit --flow-kit --icon-kit -o er.html
    ```

## Not built yet

See [PENDING.md](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/PENDING.md#flow-kit-next-phases).

# irender-icon-kit

SVG icons for [iRender](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/README.md) documents: `ui-icon`, with packs of original icons for everyday interfaces and for industries, each in an outline and a filled style, and your own packs from SVG files.

```rust
let mut engine = irender_html::Engine::new();
irender_icon_kit::register(&mut engine.registry);   // every built-in pack
```

From the CLI, add `--icon-kit` to `validate`, `render` or `components`, and list what ships with `icons`:

```sh
cargo run -p irender-cli -- render page.yaml --ui-kit --icon-kit -o page.html
cargo run -p irender-cli -- icons              # packs and icon names
cargo run -p irender-cli -- icons logistics    # one pack
cargo run -p irender-cli -- icons --json       # for tooling, or as page data
```

```yaml
- { type: ui-icon, props: { name: logistics:truck } }
- { type: ui-icon, props: { name: check, size: 16, label: Delivered }, style: { color: $color.primary } }
- { type: ui-icon, props: { name: retail:shopping-cart, variant: filled } }
```

## `ui-icon`

| prop | |
|---|---|
| `name` | `pack:icon`, e.g. `logistics:truck`, or a bare `icon`, found in the first pack that has it. Required. |
| `variant` | `outline` (default) or `filled`. |
| `size` | Number (px) or CSS length. Default `1em`, the size of the text around it. May use state. |
| `label` | Accessible name (`role="img"`, `aria-label`). Without it the icon is decorative and `aria-hidden`. |

- Strokes are always 2 grid units, the width the icons are drawn and spaced for, so there's no prop to change it.
- The icon is an inline `<svg>` drawn in `currentColor`, so `color` (or the surrounding text) sets it. `attrs`, `class` and `style` apply to the `<svg>` as usual.
- Only the icons a page uses are sent: there's no sprite or font to load.
- `name` and `variant` are resolved on the server. They can come from server data (`"{{ order.icon }}"`), but not from `state`. To switch icons in the browser (say, outline to filled when an item is selected), use `if` / `else` with one `ui-icon` in each branch.
- An unknown name is a render error that suggests close names (`unknown icon `trcuk`; did you mean `logistics:truck`?`).

## Built-in packs

| pack | contents |
|---|---|
| `core` | Everyday interface actions and objects: add, edit, delete, search, filter, settings, share, lock, users, calendar, time. |
| `arrows` | Arrows, chevrons, carets, corners, rotation, swap and move. |
| `status` | States of a task or record: done, failed, pending, blocked, draft, archived, scheduled, overdue, sync, online. |
| `logistics` | Transport, shipping and delivery: vehicles, parcels, containers, docks, routes and proof of delivery. |
| `warehouse` | Warehouse operations and inventory: racks, bins, picking, packing, stock levels, counts, lots and serials. |
| `retail` | Stores and e-commerce: carts, checkout, POS, products, promotions, orders, reviews and loyalty. |
| `manufacturing` | Factories and production: machines, tools, components, process equipment, quality, maintenance and safety. |
| `accounting` | Accounting operations: payables and receivables, accounts and entries, notes, accruals and depreciation, assets and cost centres, close and tax. |
| `agriculture` | Farming: machinery, crops, fields, irrigation, soil, livestock, beekeeping and harvest. |
| `automotive` | Road vehicles: cars, bikes and buses, mobility services, dealerships, keys and plates, parts, servicing, dashboard warnings and roadside help. |
| `aviation` | Airports and flight: aircraft, terminals, gates, runways, baggage, security and flight status. |
| `banking` | Banks and payments: branches and ATMs, cards and wallets, cash, accounts, transfers, lending, currencies and compliance. |
| `construction` | Building sites and real estate: heavy equipment, trades and tools, plans, buildings, site paperwork and safety. |
| `education` | Schools and e-learning: buildings, books and supplies, people, courses, assessment, timetables and subjects. |
| `energy` | Power and utilities: generation, renewables, the grid, meters, storage, EV charging and efficiency. |
| `finance` | Markets and accounting: charts, investing, assets and risk, ledgers and statements, budgets, tax, audit and forecasts. |
| `healthcare` | Hospitals and clinical care: facilities, instruments, medicines, vital signs, diagnostics, staff and records. |
| `hospitality` | Hotels, restaurants and leisure: rooms and keys, guest services, food and drink, dining and amenities. |
| `hr` | Human resources: hiring, people and org, payroll, time and leave, performance and learning, benefits and wellbeing. |
| `insurance` | Policies and claims: cover, premiums, claims and their status, underwriting, people and lines of insurance. |
| `it` | IT and software: servers, cloud, networking gear, development and DevOps, data, monitoring and security. |
| `legal` | Law and compliance: courts and people, contracts and signatures, evidence, rulings, privacy and intellectual property. |
| `marketing` | Marketing: campaigns, audiences and targeting, funnels and conversion, SEO, social and email, ads, brand and analytics. |
| `maritime` | Shipping and the sea: vessels, ports and berths, cargo handling, navigation, safety equipment, tides and voyages. |
| `media` | Media production and distribution: film, TV, radio and podcasts, audio and video, photography, print and news, streaming. |
| `mining` | Mines and quarries: shafts, tunnels, open pits, heavy equipment, ore, processing, geology and safety. |
| `oil-gas` | Oil and gas, upstream to downstream: rigs, wells, pipelines, refining, storage, transport, fuel and leaks. |
| `public-sector` | Government and civic services: buildings, elections, IDs and permits, emergency services, transport, streets and utilities. |
| `robotics` | Robots and automation: arms, grippers, mobile and legged robots, drones, actuators, sensors and safety. |
| `simulation` | Simulation and digital twins: models, scenarios, runs, parameters, randomness, meshes, physics and results. |
| `space` | Spaceflight and astronomy: rockets, satellites, stations, astronauts, planets, stars and ground stations. |
| `social` | Social networks, without logos: likes and votes, comments and replies, reposts and messages, following, profiles, feeds and stories, polls and moderation. |
| `sports` | Sports and fitness: trophies and venues, balls and equipment, athletes in motion, workouts and tracking, teams and officiating. |
| `telecom` | Telecom networks: towers and antennas, signal and coverage, SIMs and phones, calls and messages, fibre and plans. |

| `brands` | Logo marks of social networks and sign-in providers (see below). |

Bare names are looked up in `core`, `arrows` and `status` first, then the industry packs alphabetically, and `brands` last. Write `pack:icon` whenever two packs might have the same name. The [icon gallery](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/examples/icons/gallery.yaml) shows every icon.

More industry packs are planned; see [PENDING.md](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/PENDING.md).

### Logo marks

`brands` holds 56 logos: social networks (`facebook`, `instagram`, `x`, `threads`, `youtube`, `tiktok`, `reddit`, `discord`, `mastodon`, `bluesky`, …), messengers (`whatsapp`, `telegram`, `signal`, `wechat`, `line`, …), developer and creator sites (`github`, `gitlab`, `stack-overflow`, `dribbble`, `behance`, `medium`, `substack`, …) and sign-in providers (`google`, `apple`, `meta`, `slack`). `irender icons brands` lists them all.

```yaml
- { type: ui-button, props: { label: Login with Google, icon: brands:google, variant: outline } }
- { type: ui-icon, props: { name: brands:github, label: GitHub, size: 20 } }
```

- They aren't drawn for the kit. The paths come from [Simple Icons](https://simpleicons.org) 15.0.0 (CC0), unchanged, and are solid single-colour marks in `currentColor`. A `viewBox` of `-2 -2 28 28` gives them the same 2 px padding as the kit's icons.
- `variant: filled` draws the same mark.
- The logos are trademarks of their owners. Use them to point to those services (a profile link, "Sign in with …") and follow each brand's guidelines.
- Some brands aren't available: LinkedIn and Microsoft asked Simple Icons to remove their logos. Add them as your own pack (below) from the owners' brand kits.

### How the icons are drawn

Every built-in icon was drawn for this kit, not taken from another set, to one standard: a 24 px grid with 2 px padding, 2 px round strokes, shared keylines, a half-pixel grid, modifiers in the bottom-right corner and at most about 8 shapes. [GUIDELINES.md](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-icon-kit/GUIDELINES.md) is the full standard.

The filled style is drawn on the outline's own centrelines, filled *and* stroked, so its silhouette matches the outline's outer edge and the two swap without the icon shifting; inner details become cut-outs. Icons with nothing to fill (arrows, check, close, …) use their outline drawing for both styles; each pack lists them in `filled/_same.txt`.

To add or change an icon:

```sh
crates/irender-icon-kit/tools/icons.py lint                       # the measurable rules
crates/irender-icon-kit/tools/icons.py sheet logistics -o s.html  # a contact sheet at 96, 24 and 16 px, light and dark
crates/irender-icon-kit/tools/icons.py sheet logistics --filled -o s.html   # the filled style beside the outline
```

## Your own packs

```rust
use irender_icon_kit::{IconKit, Pack};

let brand = Pack::from_dir("brand", "assets/icons")?;      // every *.svg; `Box Truck.svg` → `box-truck`; filled ones from assets/icons/filled/
let kit = IconKit::new().with(brand);                       // built-ins first, then yours
irender_icon_kit::register_with(&mut engine.registry, kit);

// Or your names first, with only the built-in packs you want:
let kit = IconKit::empty().with(brand).with_builtin("core")?.with_builtin("logistics")?;

// Or from strings:
let mut pack = Pack::new("brand", "Brand")?;
pack.add_svg("logo", include_str!("logo.svg"))?;
pack.add_svg_filled("logo", include_str!("logo-filled.svg"))?;   // optional: `variant: filled`
pack.same_when_filled("divider")?;                               // or: the outline serves both
```

CLI: `--icons assets/icons` (a pack named after the directory) or `--icons brand=assets/icons`, repeatable; it implies `--icon-kit`.

Any SVG works, at any `viewBox`. On load it's reduced to its shapes (`path`, `circle`, `ellipse`, `rect`, `line`, `polyline`, `polygon`, `g`), their geometry and drawing attributes, and the root's `viewBox` and drawing defaults (`fill`, `stroke`, `stroke-width`, …). Scripts, styles, links, text, `<use>`, images, gradients, event attributes and `url(…)` references are dropped, so a pack file can't put anything else into a page. For icons that follow the text colour, draw them with `currentColor` (or no colour at all for fills).
